-          warning   spec.module.extra                feedback   The instrument has the module Sequence 55555555 (feedback), which the spec does not list.
-          error     spec.variable.derived-is-lookup  HasPets    The derived variable HasPets is a data lookup field: it is imported, not computed.
pets       info      spec.edit.unverifiable           age_range  The edit age_range: not verifiable (edit storage unknown).
5 error(s), 7 warning(s), 2 info.
Option Effect --spec SPEC The spec (required). --module ID Compare one module only; modules the spec does not list and variables are then not checked, and an item the module holds that the spec lists in another module is reported as extra. --instrument NAME The instrument to compare when the file has several. --edits off\|info\|strict How to check edits (below). Default: info. --format json\|table JSON (default): the spec, the instrument, a summary, each module's result and the findings; or a table. -o PATH, --indent N Where to write, and the JSON indentation. --fail-severity info\|warning\|error The least severe finding that fails the run. Default: error.

ddi conform exits with:

  • 0: no finding reaches --fail-severity;
  • 1: one does, or the spec extra is not installed;
  • 2: the comparison cannot run: the spec does not read or pass its checks, --module names no module of the spec, --edits strict and the spec has no match.edits, or the instrument file does not read.

From Python:

import ddi_l as ddi
from ddi_l.spec import conform, load_spec

report = conform(ddi.read_ddi("instrument.xml"), load_spec("pet-survey.spec.yaml"))
print(report.summary)
for finding in report.findings:
    print(
        finding.severity, finding.rule_id, finding.module, finding.item, finding.message
    )
path: Check a questionnaire against a spec

items.title: Where ids are found
items.text:
Each id is looked for in the places match lists, in order. The first place that holds an id anywhere in the instrument is the one used. An id found there on several constructs is reported as ambiguous, never guessed.

Key Default Places question_id [construct_alias, item_name, item_alias, construct_name] the alias of the question construct's r:OutParameter, the question item's name, its output alias, the construct's name statement_id [construct_name, label, user_id] the statement's ConstructName, r:Label, r:UserID module_id [construct_name, label, user_id] the same, on a sequence module_depth any depth the depth of module sequences: the instrument's own sequence is 1, its children 2 edits none how edit checks are stored, for --edits strict lookup_types none a data lookup field type and the spec type it stands for: {Text: text, Integer: numeric}

A module is a sequence. A sequence typed ConditionalChildContainer is the body of an IfThenElse branch, never a module or a page; a page is any other sequence inside a module. When several places hold different ids for one question (its construct alias and its item name, say), the question is found by the first, and spec.item.id-sources-differ says what the others hold.

A module found on several sequences is spec.module.ambiguous; none of its candidates is reported as an extra module, and the items inside them are neither misplaced nor gate-checked. An item referenced from several places is compared where the spec puts it: it is misplaced only when none of its places is in its module, and each other module holding it reports it as spec.item.extra. A referenced domain (a ManagedNumericRepresentation, say) is compared like an inline one; of a StructuredMixedResponseDomain, the one domain of the spec's kind is compared.
path: Check a questionnaire against a spec

items.title: Gates
items.text:
A module's gate is every condition on the way from the instrument to the module; a question's own gate is every condition between its module and the question. The Then branch of an IfThenElse adds its condition; an ElseIf branch adds its condition and the negation of those before it; the Else branch adds the negation of them all. With gate_scope: page, the module's gate is expected on each page instead of on the module. A statement has no gate of its own in a spec: with gate_scope: page, its page gate must be one of the gates between its module and it (spec.gate.missing or spec.gate.different otherwise), and a further gate of its own is not compared.

When the paths to an item inside its module carry gates that are not equivalent, its gate is spec.gate.unverifiable.

With the logic extra, gates and edits are decided as decide() does after their normal forms are compared, so a gate written differently that always agrees with the spec's is not reported. The spec's response domains and variable types say what each name is: a numeric domain with no decimals is a whole number, so PetCount > 0 and PetCount >= 1 agree. A gate or an edit that differs names a respondent the two disagree on, in the message and in the finding's example:

Module pets is gated by PetCount > 0; the spec says PetCount > 1 (they differ when PetCount is 1).

--semantics syntactic (conform(semantics="syntactic")) compares normal forms only, as without the extra; --semantics smt fails without it.

A Neutral condition's subjects are followed through their bindings, those of each item's latest version, to the question they come from. A question the spec does not list is named by its first id, so a gate bound to the wrong question reads as that question; one output of a question with several (a grid's cell) is named by its alias, or, when the spec does not know that alias, by the spec variable an alias on the way names. A subject bound to no question is named by the output its bindings end at (a data lookup's field): an alias never hides which question, output or field a gate is bound to. Blaise code is read with the spec's blaise words, its {{name}} inputs named the same way.
path: Check a questionnaire against a spec

items.title: Edits
items.text:
Where an instrument stores its edit checks is not known in general, so by default each edit is reported as info: not verifiable (edit storage unknown). --edits off leaves edits out.

--edits strict looks for them, once the spec says how they are stored. An edit check is a ComputationItem marked by a user attribute; its id is in one of its construct_name, label or user_id:

match:
  edits: {attribute: kind, value: EditCheck, id: construct_name}

Colectica, for instance, marks its computations with an r:UserAttributePair whose r:AttributeKey reads x:TypeOfComputation: set attribute and value to what your exports hold. An edit with no such check is spec.edit.missing; one whose condition differs from when is spec.edit.different.
path: Check a questionnaire against a spec

items.title: Rules
items.text: Rule Default Reported when spec.instrument.missing error No instrument in the file matches the spec's instrument, or the file has none. spec.instrument.ambiguous error Several instruments match; name one with instrument or --instrument. spec.module.missing error A required module is not in the instrument. spec.module.ambiguous error Several sequences carry a module's id. spec.module.extra warning A sequence at the modules' depth that the spec does not list. spec.item.missing error A question or statement is not found. spec.item.ambiguous error Several constructs carry a question's or statement's id. spec.item.extra warning A question or statement in a module that the spec does not list there, or lists in another module. spec.item.misplaced warning A question or statement found only in other modules than the spec's. spec.item.id-sources-differ info The id sources of a question disagree (its construct name and its item name, say). spec.code.missing error A code the spec lists is not offered. spec.code.extra error A code is offered the spec does not list. spec.code.label warning A code's category label differs from the spec's, in one language. spec.language.missing warning A question's or statement's text, or a code's label, lacks one of the spec's languages. spec.domain.type error The response domain is of another kind (code, numeric, text, date), or a mixed domain holds none of the spec's kind. spec.domain.length error A text domain's minimum or maximum length differs. spec.domain.range error A numeric domain's bounds, or whether they are included, differ. spec.domain.decimals warning A numeric domain's decimals differ. spec.domain.unverifiable info The question's domain cannot be read (several, a mixed domain with several of the spec's kind, a reference not in the file, a code list that cannot be resolved). spec.gate.missing error The spec gates a module or question, and nothing gates it. spec.gate.different error The gate differs from the spec's; both normal forms are shown. spec.gate.extra warning A module or question is gated, and the spec gates it with nothing. spec.gate.scope error The gate wraps each page where the spec says the module, or the reverse. spec.gate.unverifiable warning The stored gate cannot be read back into an expression (an operator code not listed, a don't-know test, and and or mixed, malformed Neutral JSON, native code this reader does not know), or paths to the item carry different gates. spec.edit.unverifiable info Not verifiable (edit storage unknown): reported for each edit unless --edits strict or off. spec.edit.missing error With --edits strict, no edit check carries the edit's id. spec.edit.different error With --edits strict, the edit check's condition differs from when. spec.variable.import-undeclared error An imported variable is not a field of any data lookup the instrument reaches. spec.variable.import-type warning An imported variable's lookup field type differs (with match.lookup_types). spec.variable.derived-is-lookup error A derived variable is a data lookup field: it is imported, not computed.
path: Check a questionnaire against a spec

items.title: Limits
items.text:
• Only the operator codes' names are known. A code not listed, and DontKnow and NotDontKnow (the expression language has no "don't know"), are reported as unverifiable.
  • How a statement treats a question with no answer is not known. ddi-l reads every comparison as false without an answer, as the expression language does.
  • The order of and and or inside a group is not known. Gates that mix them in one group are reported as unverifiable, and none is compiled that way.
  • Without the logic extra, nothing is calculated. Normalising does not prove arithmetic equivalence: x > 3 and x >= 4 are reported as different even for a whole-number question. With it, what decide() cannot model, such as text compared by order, is still compared by normal form.
  • A question compared only with = and != may take several answers, unless its domain says otherwise. Two gates that differ only for several answers (x = 1 and x = 2 and x = 1 and x = 3) are reported as different, without a respondent.
  • Where edits are stored is not known in general, hence --edits info by default.
  • A comparison under not is kept as written, since it differs from its opposite when the question has no answer.
path: Check a questionnaire against a spec

items.title: Load DDI from spreadsheets
items.text:
Many teams keep their metadata in spreadsheets: one row per variable, one per question, one per code. ddi-l loads those spreadsheets into DDI in one step, as long as they follow the layout on this page: one table per kind of item, with rows that point at each other by id.

The tables can be a folder of CSV files, the same zipped, or one Excel workbook with a sheet per table. The result is a FragmentInstance laid out as Colectica Designer writes one, or a DDI study.

Start from a template: the spreadsheet templates page has blank tables and a filled-in bilingual example, as CSV files and as an Excel workbook.

items.title: What the tables cover
items.text:
The tables cover what most organizations document about a study, from its citation to its questionnaire, variables and data files.

Area Tables DDI items The study studies, groups, organizations, individuals StudyUnit, Group, Organization, Individual Concepts concepts, universes, unit_types Concept, Universe, UnitType Variables conceptual_variables, represented_variables, variables ConceptualVariable, RepresentedVariable, Variable Codes code_lists, codes CodeList (flat or hierarchical), Category Questions instructions, questions, question_texts, question_grids, question_blocks, question_groups Instruction, QuestionItem, QuestionGrid, QuestionBlock, QuestionGroup Questionnaire instruments, flow Instrument, Sequence, QuestionConstruct, StatementItem, IfThenElse, Loop Data variable_groups, datasets, ncubes VariableGroup, PhysicalInstance, DataRelationship, NCube Methods and quality methodologies, processing_events, quality_statements Methodology, ProcessingEvent, QualityStatement Comparison comparisons ConceptMap, UniverseMap, QuestionMap, VariableMap, CategoryMap

settings holds the agency, version and language every table uses.

Use the tables you need and leave out the rest: a folder with only settings, concepts and variables is fine.

Some things are not in the tables: column positions of fixed-width files, classification levels and families, geography, sampling plans, derivation and computation code, and managed missing-value schemes. Load the tables, then add those to the typed models in Python, or in Colectica.

items.title: How the tables fit together
items.text:
A column that points at another table holds that table's ids. The diagrams show every link, one area at a time. A crow's foot marks the side that can have many rows; a column that holds several ids (a|b) makes a many-to-many link. In DDI each link is a reference, such as a variable's r:QuestionReference or a universe's r:DefiningConceptReference.

Concepts, universes and codes, and the variables they define:

erDiagram
    concepts }o--o{ concepts : "parent"
    concepts |o--o{ universes : "concept"
    concepts |o--o{ unit_types : "concept"
    concepts |o--o{ conceptual_variables : "concept"
    universes }o--o{ conceptual_variables : "universe"
    unit_types |o--o{ conceptual_variables : "unit_type"
    concepts |o--o{ represented_variables : "concept"
    unit_types |o--o{ represented_variables : "unit_type"
    conceptual_variables |o--o{ represented_variables : "conceptual_variable"
    code_lists |o--o{ represented_variables : "code_list"
    code_lists ||--o{ codes : "code_list"
    codes |o--o{ codes : "parent"

Variables, their groups, data files and n-cubes:

erDiagram
    concepts |o--o{ variables : "concept"
    universes }o--o{ variables : "universe"
    unit_types |o--o{ variables : "unit_type"
    code_lists |o--o{ variables : "code_list"
    conceptual_variables |o--o{ variables : "conceptual_variable"
    represented_variables |o--o{ variables : "represented_variable"
    questions }o--o{ variables : "question"
    datasets }o--o{ variables : "dataset"
    variable_groups }o--o{ variables : "group"
    variable_groups |o--o{ variable_groups : "parent"
    concepts |o--o{ variable_groups : "concept"
    universes }o--o{ variable_groups : "universe"
    variables }o--o{ ncubes : "dimensions"
    universes }o--o{ ncubes : "universe"

Questions, grids, blocks and groups:

erDiagram
    questions ||--o{ question_texts : "question"
    concepts |o--o{ questions : "concept"
    code_lists |o--o{ questions : "code_list"
    instructions }o--o{ questions : "instruction"
    question_groups }o--o{ questions : "group"
    concepts |o--o{ question_grids : "concept"
    code_lists |o--o{ question_grids : "rows, columns, code_list"
    instructions }o--o{ question_grids : "instruction"
    question_groups }o--o{ question_grids : "group"
    questions }o--o{ question_blocks : "questions"
    question_grids }o--o{ question_blocks : "questions"
    concepts |o--o{ question_blocks : "concept"
    instructions }o--o{ question_blocks : "instruction"
    question_groups }o--o{ question_blocks : "group"
    question_groups |o--o{ question_groups : "parent"
    concepts |o--o{ question_groups : "concept"

The questionnaire flow. A question step names a question, a grid or a block:

erDiagram
    instruments ||--o{ flow : "instrument"
    flow |o--o{ flow : "parent"
    questions |o--o{ flow : "question"
    question_grids |o--o{ flow : "question"
    question_blocks |o--o{ flow : "question"

The study, its people and what hangs from it. A creator or publisher is an organization or an individual; a study has at most one methodology:

erDiagram
    studies }o--o{ groups : "studies"
    groups |o--o{ groups : "parent"
    organizations }o--o{ studies : "creator, publisher, funder"
    individuals }o--o{ studies : "creator, publisher"
    universes |o--o{ studies : "universe"
    concepts |o--o{ studies : "concept"
    studies ||--o{ instruments : "study"
    studies ||--o{ datasets : "study"
    studies ||--o| methodologies : "study"
    studies ||--o{ processing_events : "study"
    studies ||--o{ quality_statements : "study"

Comparisons. The type column says which table source and target name; for category they name codes:

erDiagram
    concepts |o--o{ comparisons : "source, target"
    universes |o--o{ comparisons : "source, target"
    questions |o--o{ comparisons : "source, target"
    variables |o--o{ comparisons : "source, target"
    codes |o--o{ comparisons : "source, target"

items.title: Rules every table follows
items.text:
• One file or sheet per table, named as in the tables above: concepts.csv, or a sheet called concepts. The first row holds the column names; every other row is one item.
  • id is your key. Give every row an id, unique within its table: the variable name, a question number, anything without spaces. Other tables use it to point at the row: a variable's question column holds a question's id.
  • Several ids in one cell are separated by |: Q_AGE|Q_AGE_PROXY.
  • Empty cells are fine. Only the columns marked required below must be filled.
  • Notes columns are ignored. A column whose name starts with # or _ is yours, for comments or working notes.
  • Unknown columns are errors, so a misspelled lable@en is caught rather than silently dropped.
  • One study needs no study column. When studies has a single row, instruments, data files, methodologies, processing events and quality statements with an empty study belong to it.

items.title: Identifiers and versions
items.text:
Every item gets a DDI identifier (a UUID). Leave ddi_id empty and one is derived from the agency, the table and the row's id, so loading the same tables again gives the same identifiers, and a re-import updates items instead of duplicating them. Fill ddi_id to update an item that is already in Colectica, with either of:

  • its identifier, such as 4bf610ee-6771-44da-ab0b-00655b53b79b, or VS1.V1 for one scoped to its scheme;
  • its URN, such as urn:ddi:example.org:4bf610ee-6771-44da-ab0b-00655b53b79b:3. The URN's agency must be the tables' agency, and its version is the item's when the row's version is empty.

Every item takes the version from settings, unless its own version column says otherwise. A version is whole numbers separated by dots: 1, 2, 1.1.

Each value is checked as the tables are read, and one that DDI does not accept is reported with its file, row and column, with every other problem: an identifier with a space or more than one dot, a URN of another agency or missing a part, the older URN form that names object types (urn:ddi:example.org:VariableScheme:VS1:Variable:V1:1), a version such as v2, or two rows with the same identifier. The agency and version in settings, or passed in, are checked too.

items.title: Names and labels
items.text: name is the item's short name, such as AGE or Q_AGE, written in the language set in settings. It defaults to id. label and description are for people, in as many languages as you have.

items.title: Several languages
items.text:
Text that people read goes in one column per language: the column name, @, and a language tag.

Column Meaning label@en, label@fr the label in English and in French description@fr-CA the description in Canadian French text@en, text@fr a question's wording in English and in French

Any BCP 47 tag works: en, fr, fr-CA, iu. Add a column per language you document; a cell left empty means that language has no text for that row. All the languages of one row are written into one DDI element, as Colectica writes them.

items.title: Question wording for different audiences
items.text:
text@en is the wording everyone sees. When a question is worded differently for some respondents (asked of a proxy, or read by an interviewer), add one row per wording to question_texts:

question language audience text Q_WORK en proxy Last week, did this person work at a job or business? Q_WORK fr proxy La semaine dernière, cette personne a-t-elle travaillé à un emploi ou à une entreprise? Q_AGE en intvwr INTERVIEWER: Record the age in completed years.

Each wording becomes its own d:QuestionText. DDI 3.3 records who a wording is for in its audienceLanguage attribute, a language tag, so the audience is added to the language as a private-use subtag:

Wording audienceLanguage text@en in questions en proxy wording in English en-x-proxy intvwr wording in French fr-x-intvwr

Because it goes into a language tag, an audience is letters and digits, at most 8 between hyphens: proxy, intvwr, self-resp. A question can have one wording per language and audience.

items.title: Custom properties
items.text:
Any property DDI has no column for goes in a column named custom: and the property name: custom:Steward, custom:Sensitivity, custom:Mode. Each filled cell becomes an r:UserAttributePair on the item, with the key extension: and the property name, which is how Colectica Designer stores its custom fields. A name that already has a prefix, such as custom:x:Source, keeps it as it is.

Every table whose rows are items takes custom columns. Four tables do not: settings, codes (a category can be shared by several codes), question_texts and comparisons.

items.title: The questionnaire flow
items.text:
An instrument's content is in flow, one row per step, in the order the steps run. type says what a step is:

type What it is Needs question asks a question, grid or block question statement shows a text text@<language> sequence holds the steps whose parent it is, in order if runs its then steps when condition holds, else its else steps condition loop repeats its steps while condition holds condition

A step without a parent is at the top of its instrument. A step inside an if says which side it is on with branch (then by default, or else). The example's flow:

id type parent branch question condition F_INTRO statement F_DEMO sequence F_AGE question F_DEMO Q_AGE F_SEX question F_DEMO Q_SEX F_IF_15 if AGE >= 15 F_WORK question F_IF_15 then Q_WORK F_IF_WORKED if F_IF_15 then WORKED = 1 F_JOBS loop F_IF_WORKED job <= JOB_COUNT F_JOB question F_JOBS B_JOB F_TOO_YOUNG statement F_IF_15 else F_END statement

Conditions are text, recorded with the language named in condition_language (pseudo-code by default): write them in the syntax your collection system uses.

items.title: What the tables add
items.text:
Some items follow from the rows without a table of their own. Their identifiers are derived like a row's, so they too are the same on every load.

From Comes each code a category holding its labels, or the one its category key shares each study a data collection holding its instruments, methodology and processing events each study's processing events a processing event scheme listing them each instrument a sequence holding its top-level flow steps each if and loop a sequence for each of its branches or its body each dataset a data relationship with a logical record listing its variables each map of comparisons one map holding its rows

A unit type with no concept gets the placeholder concept reference Colectica writes, since the DDI 3.3 schema requires one by mistake.

items.title: Each table, column by column
items.text: Columns marked required must be present and filled on every row.

items.title: settings
items.text:
Two columns, setting and value, one row per setting:

setting Meaning Default agency the maintenance agency of every item, such as org.example required version the version of every item without its own 1 language the language of names en

items.title: Columns most tables have
items.text:
Every table whose rows are items, except studies, groups, organizations and individuals, starts with these:

Column Required What goes in it id yes your key for the row ddi_id an existing DDI identifier or URN to keep version the item's version (1, 2, 1.1), if not the one in settings name the short name; defaults to id label@<language> a short label, per language description@<language> a longer definition, per language custom:<name> a property of your own

studies, groups, organizations and individuals have id, ddi_id, version and custom columns too, and the columns listed for each.

items.title: studies
items.text:
One row per study: a survey cycle, a census, an administrative source.

Column What goes in it title@<language> the study's title; defaults to id subtitle@<language> a subtitle alternate_title@<language> another title, such as an acronym abstract@<language> what the study is about purpose@<language> why it was done creator who made it: organizations or individuals ids, or names publisher who publishes it: ids or names, as for creator publication_date when it was published: 2024, 2024-05 or 2024-05-31 identifier a persistent identifier, such as a DOI: 10.1234/abcd identifier_agency who manages the identifier: DOI, Handle, ARK... copyright@<language> its copyright statement license the licence it is published under, as a web address: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ kind_of_data Survey data, Administrative records... analysis_unit Persons, Households, Businesses... universe who the study covers, as a universes id concept the concept that defines the study, as a concepts id keywords@<language> topics, separated by vertical bars start_date, end_date the period covered: 2024-01-01 countries country codes covered, such as CA funder who funds it, as organizations ids grant_number the funding grant numbers

A creator or publisher that is an id in organizations or individuals becomes a reference to it; anything else is written as a name.

items.title: groups
items.text:
One row per group of studies, such as every cycle of a survey.

Column What goes in it title@<language> the group's title; defaults to id abstract@<language> what the group holds purpose@<language> why the studies are grouped type the kind of group: Series, Program... studies the studies in it, as studies ids parent the group it sits in, as a groups id

items.title: organizations
items.text: Column Required What goes in it name@<language> yes the organization's name, per language abbreviation a short name or acronym email a contact email address url its web site description@<language> a description, per language

items.title: individuals
items.text:
Column What goes in it first_name given name last_name family name email a contact email address url a web page description@<language> a description, per language, such as the role

At least one of first_name and last_name is needed.

items.title: concepts
items.text: Column What goes in it parent the broader concept(s) this one narrows, as concepts ids

items.title: universes
items.text: Column What goes in it concept the concept that defines the universe, as a concepts id

items.title: unit_types
items.text:
The kinds of unit described: person, household, business.

Column What goes in it concept the concept of the unit, as a concepts id

items.title: conceptual_variables
items.text:
A concept measured on a unit type, with no representation yet.

Column What goes in it concept the concept, as a concepts id universe who it describes, as universes ids unit_type the kind of unit, as a unit_types id

items.title: represented_variables
items.text:
A conceptual variable with a representation, shared by the variables that record it the same way.

Column What goes in it conceptual_variable the conceptual variable, as a conceptual_variables id concept, unit_type without a conceptual_variable: the concept and unit type representation required: code, numeric, text or datetime code_list, numeric_type, min, max, max_length, date_type as for questions

items.title: code_lists
items.text: Only the columns most tables have. The codes go in codes.

items.title: codes
items.text:
One row per code, in the order the codes are listed. Each code gets a category holding its labels.

Column Required What goes in it code_list yes the code list, as a code_lists id value yes the code as stored in the data: 1, 01, M label@<language> the category label, per language description@<language> a longer definition, per language category a key to share one category between code lists missing true for a missing-value code, such as Refusal parent for a hierarchy: the value of the code this one sits under

Codes with the same category key share one category, labelled from the first of them: a "Not stated" category used by every code list, for example.

A classification is a code list whose codes nest: give each code below the top level the value of its parent, in the same code list, and list the parent first.

code_list value label@en parent OCCUPATIONS 1 Management OCCUPATIONS 11 Senior managers 1 OCCUPATIONS 12 Middle managers 1 OCCUPATIONS 2 Sales and service

items.title: instructions
items.text:
Instructions to respondents or interviewers, attached to questions with their instruction column.

Column What goes in it text@<language> the instruction, per language

items.title: questions
items.text: Column What goes in it text@<language> the wording, per language concept the concept the question measures, as a concepts id response the kind of answer: code, numeric, text or datetime code_list for code: the code list, as a code_lists id numeric_type for numeric: Integer, Decimal, Float, Double, Long or Short min for numeric: the lowest valid value max for numeric: the highest valid value max_length for text: the longest valid answer, in characters date_type for datetime: Date, DateTime, Time, Year, YearMonth or Duration instruction instructions shown with it, as instructions ids group the question groups it belongs to, as question_groups ids

items.title: question_texts
items.text: Column Required What goes in it question yes the question, as a questions id language yes the wording's language audience who the wording is for; empty for everyone text yes the wording

items.title: question_grids
items.text:
A question asked for each row of a grid: rows from one code list, columns from another if any, and one response per cell.

Column What goes in it text@<language> the question, per language rows required: the rows, as a code_lists id columns the columns, as a code_lists id response and its details the answer in each cell, as for questions concept, instruction, group as for questions

items.title: question_blocks
items.text:
Questions presented together.

Column What goes in it intent@<language> what the block is for questions its questions in order, as questions or question_grids ids concept, instruction, group as for questions

items.title: question_groups
items.text:
Groups of questions, such as the modules of a questionnaire. Questions, grids and blocks join with their group column.

Column What goes in it type the kind of group: Module, Topic... parent the group it sits in, as a question_groups id concept the concept it covers, as a concepts id

items.title: instruments
items.text:
One row per questionnaire. Its content is in flow.

Column What goes in it study the study, as a studies id type the kind of instrument: CAWI, CATI, Paper...

items.title: flow
items.text:
The steps of each instrument, as explained in The questionnaire flow.

Column Required What goes in it instrument yes the instrument, as an instruments id type yes question, statement, sequence, if or loop parent the sequence, if or loop it is inside, as a flow id branch inside an if: then or else; defaults to then question for question: a questions, question_grids or question_blocks id text@<language> for statement: the text shown condition for if and loop: the condition, such as AGE >= 15 condition_language the language of the condition; defaults to pseudo-code

items.title: variables
items.text:
Column What goes in it concept the concept the variable measures, as a concepts id universe who the variable describes, as universes ids question the question(s) its values come from, as questions ids representation how values are recorded: code, numeric, text or datetime code_list, numeric_type, min, max, max_length, date_type as for questions unit_type the kind of unit, as a unit_types id conceptual_variable its conceptual variable, as a conceptual_variables id represented_variable its represented variable, as a represented_variables id dataset the data file(s) it is a column of, as datasets ids group its variable groups, as variable_groups ids

A variable with an empty representation takes the one of its represented variable, or else the response of its first question, so a variable fed by a coded question does not repeat the code list. A data file lists its variables in the order of the variables table.

items.title: variable_groups
items.text:
Groups of variables, such as topics. Variables join with their group column.

Column What goes in it type the kind of group: Topic, Derived... parent the group it sits in, as a variable_groups id concept the concept it covers, as a concepts id universe who its variables describe, as universes ids

items.title: datasets
items.text:
One row per data file. Variables join with their dataset column.

Column What goes in it title@<language> the file's title; defaults to name file where the file is: a path or URL study the study, as a studies id

In DDI a physical instance has no label, so label and description describe the file's record of variables (its logical record).

items.title: ncubes
items.text:
Multidimensional tables of aggregates.

Column What goes in it dimensions required: its dimensions in order, as variables ids purpose@<language> what the n-cube is for universe who it describes, as universes ids

items.title: methodologies
items.text:
How a study's data were collected. A study has at most one methodology.

Column What goes in it study the study, as a studies id data_collection@<language> how data were collected time_method@<language> cross-section, panel, time series... sampling@<language> how the sample was drawn deviation@<language> how the sample departs from its design weighting@<language> how weights were derived

items.title: processing_events
items.text:
What was done to a study's data after collection.

Column What goes in it study the study, as a studies id control@<language> checks made on the data cleaning@<language> how the data were cleaned or edited weighting@<language> how the data were weighted appraisal@<language> response rates, sampling error...

items.title: quality_statements
items.text: Column What goes in it study the study, as a studies id text@<language> the statement

items.title: comparisons
items.text:
How items compare, across studies or cycles: one row per pair. Rows with the same map form one map.

Column Required What goes in it map yes your key for the map the row belongs to type yes what is compared: concept, universe, question, variable or category source yes the item compared from, as an id in that table target yes the item compared to, as an id in that table commonality@<language> what they share difference@<language> how they differ weight how alike they are, from 0 to 1

For category, write code_list/value (SEX_CODES/1), or a category key of codes.

items.title: Load the tables
items.text:
From Python, load_tables() reads a folder of CSV files or a workbook and gives back typed models you can check or edit before writing:

from ddi_l.tables import load_tables, write_table_templates

# The bilingual example from the templates page, written to a folder.
write_table_templates("my-survey", example=True)

tables = load_tables("my-survey")
print(len(tables.variables))  # -> 5
print(tables.get("variables", "AGE").labels[1].text)  # -> Âge en années
print(len(tables.tables["flow"]))  # -> 16

# A Colectica FragmentInstance, one item per fragment.
tables.to_fragment().save("my-survey.xml")

tables.tables holds the items of each table, and those it implies, in row order: the 16 items of flow are its 11 steps and the 5 sequences they imply. tables.items holds them all.

The same tables as one Excel workbook load the same way:

from pathlib import Path

write_table_templates("my-survey.xlsx", example=True, layout="xlsx")
tables = load_tables("my-survey.xlsx")

# A zip of the CSV files, at its top or in one folder, loads too.
write_table_templates("my-survey.zip", example=True, layout="zip")
tables = load_tables("my-survey.zip")

# So do the bytes of a workbook or a zip, received from an upload: they are
# read in memory, and problems name them workbook.xlsx or tables.zip.
tables = load_tables(Path("my-survey.xlsx").read_bytes())

load_tables() takes agency=, version= and language= to override settings.

items.title: A fragment or a study document
items.text:
to_fragment() writes every item, whatever the tables. Its top-level item is the only group, or else the only study; pass top_level= to choose another.

to_study() puts the items inside a new study of a DDIInstance document. A study document has one study and no place for groups, people, variable groups, processing events, quality statements or comparisons, so it takes the other tables only, and says which tables to remove otherwise:

from pathlib import Path

folder = Path("questionnaire")
folder.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
(folder / "settings.csv").write_text(
    "setting,value\nagency,example.org\n", encoding="utf-8"
)
(folder / "concepts.csv").write_text("id,label@en\nAGE,Age\n", encoding="utf-8")
(folder / "variables.csv").write_text(
    "id,concept,representation,numeric_type\nAGE,AGE,numeric,Integer\n",
    encoding="utf-8",
)

study = load_tables(folder).to_study("Labour Force Survey")
print(study.validate())  # -> []
study.save("labour-force-survey.xml")

From the command line:

ddi tables template my-survey --example        # the example, as CSV files
ddi tables import my-survey -o my-survey.xml   # a Colectica FragmentInstance
ddi tables import questionnaire --study "Labour Force Survey" -o study.xml

Over HTTP, ddi serve offers the same: POST /v1/tables/import takes a workbook or a zip and answers with the fragment, or with every problem as a 422; GET /v1/tables/template gives the templates, and GET /v1/tables describes every table and column as JSON.

items.title: When something is wrong
items.text:
Loading checks every table before writing anything, and reports every problem at once, each with its file (or sheet), row and column:

Error: my-survey has 3 problems:
  - variables.csv, row 4, column question: no row in questions has id 'Q_AGEE'
  - codes.csv, row 7, column missing: 'maybe' is not true or false
  - flow.csv, row 6, column parent: 'F_AGE' is a question step; only a
    sequence, if or loop holds other steps

Row numbers are the spreadsheet's, header included, so row 4 is the fourth row you see in Excel.

items.title: Excel tips
items.text:
• Keep codes and dates as text. Excel turns 01 into the number 1 and 2024-05 into a date. The template workbooks format every cell as text; in your own workbook, format the columns as Text before typing.
  • Save CSV as "CSV UTF-8", so accented letters survive. Files saved with semicolons by a French-language Excel are read too.
  • One workbook or one folder. In a workbook, a sheet named README, or with a name starting with _, is ignored; any other sheet must be one of the tables.

items.title: Into Colectica
items.text: The FragmentInstance from to_fragment() is written the way Colectica Designer writes an export, with one item per <Fragment>, for importing into a Colectica repository; try the import in a test repository first. See Work with Colectica exports for reading and editing such files. Because identifiers are derived from your ids, loading the same tables again after editing them gives the same items with the same identifiers: bump version in settings (or per row) and import again.

items.title: Spreadsheet templates
items.text: Templates for the tables described in Load DDI from spreadsheets. Each comes as an Excel workbook (one sheet per table, plus a README sheet listing every column) and as a zip of CSV files (one file per table, plus README.txt).

items.title: Example
items.text:
A small bilingual (English and French) labour survey with every table filled in: the study with its series, agency and manager; concepts, a universe, a unit type and the variable cascade; code lists sharing a "Not stated" category and a two-level occupation classification; questions with proxy and interviewer wordings, an instruction, a grid, a block and modules; a web questionnaire with a sequence, nested conditions and a loop; variables in groups and in a data file; an n-cube; methodology, processing and quality; a concept comparison across cycles; and custom properties.

Example workbook Example CSV files

Load it as it is to see what each row becomes:

ddi tables import ddi-tables-example.xlsx -o example.xml
ddi tables import ddi-tables-example.zip -o example.xml   # the zip loads as it is

items.title: Blank
items.text:
The same tables with headers only, with label, description and text columns for English and French. Fill agency in settings, delete the tables you do not need, and add rows.

Blank workbook Blank CSV files

items.title: Other languages
items.text:
For other languages, generate the blank tables with the columns you need:

ddi tables template my-tables --lang en --lang fr --lang iu --format xlsx

Or from Python:

from ddi_l.tables import write_table_templates

write_table_templates("my-tables", languages=("en", "es"))

--format (or layout=) is csv for a folder of CSV files, zip for the same zipped, or xlsx for a workbook.

items.title: What is in a template
items.text:
Sheet or file One row per README column, with what goes in it (workbook only; README.txt in the zip) settings setting: agency, version, language studies study groups group of studies organizations organization individuals person concepts concept universes universe unit_types kind of unit conceptual_variables conceptual variable represented_variables represented variable code_lists code list codes code instructions instruction questions question question_texts extra wording of a question, by language and audience question_grids grid question question_blocks block of questions question_groups question group or module instruments questionnaire flow step of a questionnaire variables variable variable_groups variable group datasets data file ncubes n-cube methodologies methodology processing_events processing event quality_statements quality statement comparisons pair of compared items

Every cell of the workbooks is formatted as text, so codes such as 01 keep their leading zero. The CSV files are UTF-8 with a byte-order mark, so Excel opens accented letters correctly.

items.title: User guide
items.text:
This guide walks you through the main features of the ddi-l CRUD API. Each section is self-contained, so you can jump to the workflow you need.

Prerequisites

  • Python 3.11 or newer with ddi-l installed (pip install ddi-l).
  • No XML knowledge is required for the simple API.

items.title: How a study fits together
items.text:
A DDI study (a StudyUnit) keeps its metadata in modules, the boxes below: concepts and universes in a ConceptualComponent, the questionnaire and its questions in a DataCollection, variables, code lists and categories in a LogicalProduct, record layouts in a PhysicalDataProduct, each data file in a PhysicalInstance, and organizations and people in an Archive. Items refer to each other across modules (dashed arrows): a variable to the question that collected it, the concept it measures, its universe and its code list; a data file to the record layout and the logical record that list its variables.

flowchart TB
    accTitle: How a DDI study fits together
    accDescr: A StudyUnit holds its metadata in modules: concepts and universes in a ConceptualComponent; the instrument, its control constructs and the questions in a DataCollection; variables, code lists, categories and data relationships in a LogicalProduct; record layouts in a PhysicalDataProduct; each data file in a PhysicalInstance; organizations and individuals in an Archive. Dashed arrows are references: a variable refers to its question, concept, universe and code list; a data file refers to its record layout and data relationship, which list its variables.
    subgraph SU["StudyUnit"]
        direction TB
        subgraph CC["ConceptualComponent"]
            CON[Concept]
            UNI[Universe]
        end
        subgraph DC["DataCollection"]
            INS[Instrument]
            CTL["Sequence, IfThenElse,\nQuestionConstruct..."]
            QI[QuestionItem]
        end
        subgraph LP["LogicalProduct"]
            VAR[Variable]
            CL[CodeList]
            CAT[Category]
            DR["DataRelationship\n(LogicalRecord)"]
        end
        subgraph PDP["PhysicalDataProduct"]
            RL[RecordLayout]
        end
        subgraph PI["PhysicalInstance"]
            DF["DataFileIdentification\n(the data file)"]
        end
        subgraph AR["Archive"]
            ORG["Organization,\nIndividual"]
        end
    end
    INS -.->|ControlConstructReference| CTL
    CTL -.->|QuestionReference| QI
    QI -.->|ConceptReference| CON
    QI -.->|"CodeDomain:\nCodeListReference"| CL
    VAR -.->|QuestionReference| QI
    VAR -.->|ConceptReference| CON
    VAR -.->|UniverseReference| UNI
    VAR -.->|"CodeRepresentation:\nCodeListReference"| CL
    CL -.->|"Code:\nCategoryReference"| CAT
    DR -.->|VariableUsedReference| VAR
    RL -.->|"DataItem:\nVariableReference"| VAR
    PI -.->|RecordLayoutReference| RL
    PI -.->|DataRelationshipReference| DR

items.title: Create a study
items.text:
Use ddi.new_study() to create a new DDI document with a study unit:

import ddi_l as ddi

doc = ddi.new_study(title="Household Survey", agency="example.org")
print(doc.agency)  # -> example.org

The function returns a Document object. It automatically creates the DDI instance, study unit, and all required identification metadata.

items.title: Add questions
items.text:
Use doc.add_question() to add questions to the study:

q1 = doc.add_question(text="What is your gender?")
q2 = doc.add_question(text="How old are you?")
q3 = doc.add_question(text="What is your household income?")

print(f"Questions: {len(doc.questions)}")  # -> 3

Each question is a QuestionItem in a QuestionScheme inside the DataCollection module.

items.title: Add variables
items.text:
Use doc.add_variable() to add variables, optionally linking them to questions or concepts:

age_concept = doc.add_concept(name="Age")

doc.add_variable(name="Gender", question=q1)
doc.add_variable(name="Age", question=q2, concept=age_concept)
doc.add_variable(name="Household Income", question=q3)

print(f"Variables: {len(doc.variables)}")  # -> 3

When you pass a question= or concept= argument, ddi-l automatically creates the DDI reference linking the variable to that item.

items.title: Add concepts and universes
items.text:
demo_concept = doc.add_concept(name="Demographics")
doc.add_universe(name="Canadian adults aged 18+")

print(f"Concepts: {len(doc.concepts)}")  # -> 2
print(f"Universes: {len(doc.universes)}")  # -> 1

items.title: Add code lists
items.text:
cl = doc.add_code_list(name="Gender Codes")
print(f"Code lists: {len(doc.code_lists)}")  # -> 1

items.title: Work with any item type
items.text:
The add_item() method supports all 30 DDI item types registered in the type registry. Use it for types that do not have a dedicated convenience method:

from ddi_l.models.logicalproduct import Category, RepresentedVariable
from ddi_l.models.datacollection import Instrument

doc.add_item(Category, name="Male")
doc.add_item(Category, name="Female")
doc.add_item(RepresentedVariable, name="Gender Representation")
doc.add_item(Instrument, name="CAWI Questionnaire")

# Query items by type
print(f"Categories: {len(doc.items(Category))}")  # -> 2

items.title: Find and remove items
items.text:
Every item gets a unique identifier when created. Use find() to look up an item by its identifier, and remove() to delete it:

cat = doc.add_item(Category, name="Not specified")
print(cat.identifier)

found = doc.find(cat.identifier)
print(found)  # Prints the Category object

doc.remove(cat.identifier)
print(doc.find(cat.identifier))  # -> None

items.title: Save to XML
items.text:
doc.save("household-survey.xml")

The output uses proper DDI namespace prefixes (r:, s:, d:, l:, c:, a:, p:), not generic ns0/ns1.

items.title: Open an existing file
items.text:
doc = ddi.open_ddi("household-survey.xml")

print(f"Questions: {len(doc.questions)}")
print(f"Variables: {len(doc.variables)}")

for v in doc.variables:
    print(f"  {v.identifier}")

Save it again and the parts you did not change are written as they were read, byte for byte; only what you added or changed is laid out, with the file's own indentation. To lay the whole file out afresh, use ddi.write_ddi(doc, "out.xml", layout="default").

Pass validate=True to run schema validation on load:

doc = ddi.open_ddi("household-survey.xml", validate=True)

items.title: Validate
items.text:
Call doc.validate() to check the document against the DDI schema:

issues = doc.validate()
if issues:
    for issue in issues:
        print(f"[{issue.severity}] {issue.message}")
else:
    print("Document is valid!")

For more validation options, see the validation guide.

items.title: Advanced: working with the model layer
items.text:
The generated model classes under ddi_l.models are the advanced layer. You can import and use them directly for fine-grained control:

from ddi_l.models.base import InternationalString, Reference
from ddi_l.models.logicalproduct import Variable

var = Variable(
    agency="example.org",
    identifier="var-age",
    version="1.0",
    names=[InternationalString(text="Age", lang="en")],
)

See the models reference for a complete list of available types.

items.title: Validate and lint DDI content
items.text:
ddi-l checks documents in two ways: schema validation against the DDI XSDs, and lint rules for problems the schema allows (missing labels, broken references, agency rules).

Prerequisites

  • Python 3.11 or newer with ddi-l installed.
  • Access to the bundled schemas (installed automatically with the package).

items.title: Validate on load
items.text:
Pass validate=True when opening a document to run schema validation immediately:

import ddi_l as ddi

doc = ddi.open_ddi("my-study.xml", validate=True)

If the document fails validation, a DDIValidationError is raised.

items.title: Validate an existing document
items.text:
Call doc.validate() on any Document to check it against the DDI schema:

doc = ddi.new_study(title="Test", agency="example.org")
doc.add_question(text="How old are you?")

issues = doc.validate()
if issues:
    for issue in issues:
        print(f"[{issue.severity}] {issue.message}")
else:
    print("Document is valid!")

items.title: How schema validation runs
items.text:
Every error is reported, with the same message and path whichever way it runs. schema_loader.validate(..., backend=...) picks the way for one call; the best available is the default:

  • native, on the native backend: one pass over the document checks it against a compiled form of the schema. A valid document is done; xmlschema is not even loaded. For each element that may be wrong, xmlschema checks that element alone and words its errors, which also carry the line the element starts on. On a 9 MB export: 0.09 s when it is valid, 0.13 s with an error (2.6 s on the first call, which loads xmlschema).
  • lxml, with lxml installed: libxml2 confirms a valid document quickly; if it finds a problem, xmlschema validates the whole document again to report it (6.5 s with one error on the same export).
  • python: xmlschema validates the whole document.

items.title: High-level validation
items.text:
The ddi_l.validation module provides validate_document() for combined schema and lint validation:

from ddi_l.validation import validate_document

report = validate_document(doc)
print(f"Schema issues: {len(report.schema_issues)}")
print(f"Lint findings: {len(report.lint_findings)}")

if report.has_errors():
    print("Document has errors!")

items.title: Model-level validation
items.text:
Individual model objects can be validated with their .validate() method:

from ddi_l.models.logicalproduct import Variable
from ddi_l.models.base import InternationalString

var = Variable(
    agency="example.org",
    identifier="var-1",
    version="1.0",
    labels=[InternationalString(text="Age")],
)
var.validate()  # raises ModelValidationError on failure

items.title: Lint rules
items.text:
The lint engine runs configurable rules against documents. Use run_lint() to check referential integrity and other quality rules:

from ddi_l.document import DDIDocument
from ddi_l.lint import run_lint

doc = DDIDocument.from_xml("my-study.xml")
findings = run_lint(doc, rules=["ddi.reference.integrity"])
for f in findings:
    print(f"[{f.severity}] {f.message}")

Without rules=, run_lint() runs the default profile, DDI_PROFILE_DEFAULT. run_profile(doc, name) runs a named profile instead; ddi lint --list-profiles lists them.

Rule Severity Reports ddi.agency.allowed error A missing agency, or one outside the configured allow-list ddi.citation.present error A DDIInstance without a citation ddi.citation.title.present error A citation without a title ddi.citation.title.languages warning A citation title missing a required language ddi.maintainable.labels warning An item without an r:Label ddi.reference.integrity error (warning in a fragment) A reference whose item is not in the file ddi.reference.version warning A reference whose item is in the file, but not at the version named ddi.reference.provenance-external info A BasedOn or user-attribute reference to an item outside the file colectica.maintainable.labels warning An item with no label or name with text (colectica-questionnaire profile only)

Every finding has one of three severities: error, warning or info. info reports something worth knowing that is not a defect, and never fails ddi lint unless you pass --fail-severity info. A rule that yields any other severity raises ValueError.

A rule you add with register_rule() joins the default profile unless you pass default=False, for a rule meant only for a named profile. The colectica-questionnaire profile is for Colectica exports; see Work with Colectica exports. The lint rule reference lists every rule.

items.title: CLI validation
items.text:
From the command line:

ddi validate my-study.xml              # Schema validation
ddi lint my-study.xml                  # Lint checks
ddi lint export.xml --profile colectica-questionnaire
ddi lint my-study.xml --fail-severity warning   # Fail on warnings too
ddi validate *.xml                     # Validate multiple files

ddi lint exits non-zero when a finding reaches --fail-severity: error (the default), warning or info.

The output is JSON with message, xpath, and context fields for each issue found.

items.title: Error types
items.text:
Exception When it is raised DDIValidationError Schema validation fails (via validate=True or validate_document()) ModelValidationError A model object fails business rule checks DDIReadError The instance cannot be read DDIParseError The XML is malformed (a DDIReadError; carries line and column) DDIWriteError Serialization cannot complete DDIReferenceError A reference or study identifier cannot be resolved (a LookupError) DuplicateIdentifierError An item is added with an identifier already in the document (a ValueError)

Document.save() also issues a DDIReferenceWarning when a reference in the study points at an item the document does not contain. Filter it like any warning category:

import warnings

from ddi_l import DDIReferenceWarning

warnings.simplefilter("error", DDIReferenceWarning)  # fail instead of warn

items.title: Documentation assets
items.text: Branding and styling assets used by the documentation site.

items.title: Logo and favicon
items.text:
The header mark lives at docs/overrides/.icons/ddi/logo.svg: stacked records wrapped by an open circular arrow, for a dataset moving through the DDI Lifecycle. It is drawn entirely in currentColor, so it takes the header's foreground in light, dark and high-contrast modes without a second asset. That only works because theme.icon.logo makes the theme inline it; set as theme.logo it would load as an <img>, where currentColor is black. Do not add palette-specific fills to it.

favicon.svg is a separate file rather than the same one reused. A browser tab renders at 16–32px against the browser's chrome, not the site's, so there is no inherited colour to take: it carries its own ground and drops the lifecycle arc, which turns to mud at that size.

items.title: Colours
items.text:
There is one brand colour, blue, for links, buttons and the active page. Orange marks only the keyboard focus ring. Code blocks and inline code sit on a neutral grey with no border.

The header toggle cycles through three settings: follow the system, light (default) and dark (slate). There is no high-contrast palette to choose: readers whose system asks for more contrast (prefers-contrast: more) get darker text, stronger borders and plainer backgrounds in either scheme, and Windows high contrast (forced-colors) gets the system's own colours. Blue with a sparingly used orange is a pairing that readers with any common colour-vision deficiency can tell apart, so there are no separate colour-vision palettes. Every palette entry in zensical.toml declares primary = "custom" and accent = "custom"; without them the theme's own palette overrides palette.css.

items.title: Stylesheets
items.text:
File Purpose palette.css Colour tokens for light and dark, the more-contrast and forced-colours adjustments, and the note/info boxes. site.css Headings, the focus ring, reduced motion, the announcement bar, cards, and the landing page's hero and terminal.

The landing page's hero is docs/overrides/home.html, filled from the hero: front matter of docs/index.en.md and docs/index.fr.md.

items.title: Training curriculum
items.text:
Welcome to the ddi-l training curriculum. This course teaches you how to document surveys, censuses, and datasets using the DDI standard and Python. No prior experience with DDI or XML is needed.

This is the place to learn ddi-l step by step. The user guide is a one-page reference of the same API, and the how-to guides cover single tasks once you know the basics.

What this course covers

You will learn to turn a CSV or Excel file into a fully documented DDI package, complete with questions, variables, concepts, code lists, custom properties, versioning, and validation.

items.title: How the course is organized
items.text:
The curriculum has 17 modules in three tiers. Each module lists its prerequisites at the top, and the table below repeats them: most modules need only the one before, but some need more. You check your work from Module 3 onwards, and by the end of Tier 1 you can open, change and validate any DDI file.

Four optional modules follow: two for those who use one of ddi-l's extras, and two on the other DDI standards, DDI-Codebook and DDI-CDI. None is needed for the capstone, and the schedules below leave them out.

The times are the ones each module gives: working alone (self-paced), or in a class with an instructor (instructor-led).

# Module Self-paced Instructor-led Prerequisites Tier 1: Foundations 1 What is metadata? 30 min 45 min None 2 Set up your environment 20 min 30 min Module 1 3 Create your first study 30 min 45 min Module 2 4 Variables and questions 30 min 40 min Module 3 5 Concepts and universes 30 min 40 min Module 4 6 Open and modify files 30 min 40 min Module 5 7 Validate from the command line 30 min 40 min Module 6 Tier 2: Real-world skills 8 From CSV/Excel to DDI 45 min 60 min Module 7 9 Code lists 40 min 50 min Module 8 10 Questionnaire flows 50 min 60 min Module 9 11 Data lineage 60 min 75 min Module 10 12 Data linkage 60 min 75 min Module 11 13 Properties, find, and validate 40 min 50 min Module 12 14 Custom fields 45 min 55 min Module 13 15 Update and version 65 min 75 min Module 14 Tier 3: Applied practice 16 Advanced questionnaire specification 75 min 90 min Modules 7, 10 and 15 17 Capstone projects 60-90 min 90 min All (1-16) Optional modules 18 Decide gates exactly (logic extra) 45 min 60 min Module 16 19 Serve ddi-l over HTTP (server extra) 45 min 60 min Module 7 20 From DDI-Codebook to DDI-Lifecycle, built for reuse 60 min 75 min Modules 9 and 15 21 Describe your data with DDI-CDI 60 min 75 min Module 9

Each module starts with numbered learning objectives (O1, O2, ...): what you can do by the end of it, such as write a script or validate a file. Each exercise and quiz question is tagged with the objectives it practises, for example Exercise 2 (O3). Each module ends with a Check yourself list, one line per objective. Tick each line before you move on; for a line you cannot tick, redo the exercises with that tag.

items.title: Where do I start?
items.text:
Pick the row that fits you best.

I am a... Start at I can skim Spend extra time on University student (new to data) Module 1 Nothing Modules 3-5 Researcher (know Python, not DDI) Module 1 Module 2 Modules 1, 4 and 5: what DDI calls things Archivist (know DDI, not Python) Module 1 Module 1 Modules 2-7: the Python you need; Module 20 if your holdings are in DDI-Codebook NSO staff (know both) Module 2 Modules 1 and 3 Modules 8-16 Developer automating DDI checks Module 2 Modules 1, 4 and 5 Modules 3 and 7, then the automation track below

items.title: Automation track
items.text:
For teams that add DDI validation to pipelines or build services on ddi-l. Take Modules 2, 3 and 7, then work through these guides in order:

Session Focus Pages Pipeline foundations (45 min) Run and configure validation and lint Validate and lint DDI content, CLI recipes Automation (45 min) Script the CLI, keep reports, fail CI on errors Command-line automation playbook, Schema troubleshooting clinic Reuse and integration (45 min) Share fragments, call ddi-l from other systems Fragment reuse lab, Module 19: Serve ddi-l over HTTP, Build tools and applications

Review the performance playbook before planning large batch runs.

items.title: The big picture
items.text:
This is the process you will learn:

CSV / Excel / SQL table
        ↓
  Python script (ddi-l)
        ↓
  DDI XML document
        ↓
  Validate & version
        ↓
  Archive or publish

items.title: Suggested schedules
items.text:
Each total adds up the modules' own times, without breaks or setup.

Format Modules Instructor-led Self-paced Half-day workshop 1-5 3 h 20 min 2 h 20 min Full-day workshop 1-9 6 h 30 min 4 h 45 min Three-day intensive 1-17 16 h (about 5 h 20 min a day) 12 h 20 min to 12 h 50 min Self-paced One module per session Not applicable 12 h 20 min to 12 h 50 min over 17 sessions: 3 to 4 weeks at one session per weekday

To finish Tier 1 in a workshop, add Modules 6 and 7 to the half-day (1 h 20 min more, 4 h 40 min in all): that is a short day rather than a half-day.

  • User guide: The Document API on one page
