items.title: Answer keys
items.text:
Every exercise solution and quiz answer in the curriculum, on one page, for instructors. Learners working through a module can open the answer under each exercise and question instead.

This page is built from the modules each time the site is generated, so it always matches them.

items.title: Module 1: What is metadata and why does it matter?
Exercises
items.text:
Exercise 1

Any three of these, or similar:

  1. What does each column mean? (Is A an age? In years or months?)
  2. What unit is column C in? (Dollars? Euros? Per year or per month?)
  3. Who was surveyed? (Students? Adults? Everyone?)
  4. When was the data collected?

Exercise 2

  1. Metadata is information that describes data: what it means, where it came from, and how it was collected.
  2. Metadata: any two of the title "Campus Sleep Study 2025", the collection date (September 2025), the population (first-year students), the column name sleep_hrs, or its meaning (hours of sleep on a typical school night). Data: any of the values 7, 6, or 8.

Exercise 3

1-c, 2-d, 3-b, 4-a.

  • Findable (c): the catalog can only find what is described in structured fields.
  • Accessible (d): a standard, open format needs no special software.
  • Interoperable (b): a shared code list means the same code has the same meaning in both surveys, so the data can be combined.
  • Re-usable (a): a new user knows exactly what the data contains.

Exercise 4

For example: "DDI, the Data Documentation Initiative, is an international standard for describing surveys, censuses, and datasets in XML. National statistics offices, data archives, universities, and research teams use it so that others can find, understand, and reuse their data."

Any two of these kinds of organizations are correct: national statistics offices, data archives or national libraries, universities and their research repositories, research teams.

Exercise 5

Does: 1, 3, and 5. Does not: 2 and 4.

For example: "ddi-l creates, reads, updates, and validates DDI metadata from Python, but it does not collect survey answers."

items.title: Quiz
items.text:
Question 1 (O1): A spreadsheet has a column headed Age (years) with the values 34, 28, and 45. Which of these is metadata?

B. Metadata is information about data. The header tells you what the numbers mean and how they are measured. The values themselves, and anything computed from them, are data.

Question 2 (O2): A colleague sends a table with columns A, B, and C and no notes. Column C holds values like 52000. You want to report the average income. Which question must you answer first?

D. Without knowing that C is income, and whether it is in dollars or euros, per year or per month, any average you report could be wrong. The other questions do not change what the numbers mean.

Question 3 (O3): Which sentence best describes DDI?

A. DDI is a standard: a set of agreed rules for documentation. Option C confuses DDI with tools; ddi-l is a Python package that works with DDI, and it does not compute statistics.

Question 4 (O4): Your survey and a survey in France use the same DDI code list for gender, so the two datasets can be merged. Which FAIR principle does this support most directly?

C. Interoperable means data works with other data. A shared code list gives each code the same meaning in both datasets, so they can be combined and compared.

Question 5 (O4): A data catalog reads the title, agency, and concepts in your DDI file, so a search for 'mental health survey' lists your dataset. Which FAIR principle does this support?

A. Findable means people can discover the data. Structured DDI fields give catalogs something reliable to index and search.

Question 6 (O5): Which of these tasks does ddi-l NOT do?

B. ddi-l works with metadata: it creates, reads, updates, and validates DDI documents. Collecting answers is the job of a survey tool.

items.title: Module 2: Set up your Python environment
Exercises
items.text:
Exercise 1

For example, Python 3.12.3: yes, because 3.12 is 3.11 or newer. If you see Python 3.10.12 or older, the answer is no: install a newer Python from https://www.python.org/downloads/ before you continue.

Exercise 2

The last line starts with Successfully installed and lists ddi-l-... among the packages (the version may vary). If the packages were already installed, pip says Requirement already satisfied instead. Both mean you are ready. A line starting with ERROR means the install failed.

Exercise 3

The installed version, such as 0.1.0 or later. If you see ModuleNotFoundError instead, ddi-l is not installed in this Python: go back to Exercise 2.

Exercise 4

  1. validate ("Validate an XML document against the DDI schema.")
  2. lint ("Lint a DDI document and report findings as JSON.")
  3. versions ("List supported DDI schema releases.")

Exercise 5

  1. Python REPL: it is the quickest way to run one line you do not need to keep.
  2. Script file: it saves your code, and python my_script.py runs it again from the top.
  3. Notebook: it shows notes, code, and output together, step by step.

Other choices are fine if your reason holds up; for example, a notebook also saves your code for task 2.

items.title: Quiz
items.text:
Question 1 (O1): python --version prints Python 3.10.12. What should you do before you install ddi-l?

B. ddi-l requires Python 3.11 or newer, and 3.10 is older. Install a newer Python, then install ddi-l with it.

Question 2 (O2): The last line of pip install ddi-l pandas openpyxl reads Requirement already satisfied. What does this mean?

D. Requirement already satisfied means the package is already there. A failed install ends with a line that starts with ERROR.

Question 3 (O3): You run import ddi_l as ddi and get ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ddi_l'. What is the most likely cause?

A. Python cannot find the package, so it is not installed for this Python. Run pip install ddi-l again, or python3 -m pip install ddi-l if you start Python with python3. Option B is not valid Python: a hyphen cannot appear in an import name, which is why the module is called ddi_l.

Question 4 (O4): You want to check a file against the DDI schema from the terminal. Which command from the ddi --help list do you use?

C. Its description reads "Validate an XML document against the DDI schema." roundtrip re-writes a file, to-json converts it, and serve runs the HTTP API.

Question 5 (O5): You will build a study over several days and want to run the whole thing again from the top with one command after each change. Which workspace fits best?

B. A script file keeps your code, and one command runs all of it again. The REPL forgets what you typed when you close it.

items.title: Module 3: Create your first DDI study
Exercises
items.text:
Exercise 1

import ddi_l as ddi

doc = ddi.new_study(title="Student Well-Being Survey", agency="university.edu")

q1 = doc.add_question(text="What is your age?")
q2 = doc.add_question(text="How would you rate your health?")
q3 = doc.add_question(text="How many hours do you sleep per night?")

print(f"Questions: {len(doc.questions)}")  # -> Questions: 3
for q in doc.questions:
    print(q.identifier)

doc.save("well-being.xml")

Exercise 2

The question text sits in a <d:Text> element, inside <d:LiteralText> inside <d:QuestionText>:

<d:Text xml:lang="en" isPlainText="true">What is your age?</d:Text>

Exercise 3

from ddi_l.models.base import InternationalString

print(f"Schema problems: {len(doc.validate())}")  # -> Schema problems: 0
print(f"Lint findings: {len(doc.lint())}")  # -> Lint findings: 3

q1.labels.append(InternationalString(text="Age", lang="en"))
q2.labels.append(InternationalString(text="Self-rated health", lang="en"))
q3.labels.append(InternationalString(text="Hours of sleep", lang="en"))

print(f"Lint findings: {len(doc.lint())}")  # -> Lint findings: 0
doc.save("well-being.xml")

The three warnings were "Maintainable element is missing a label.", one per question. A label fixes each one.

Exercise 4

q1.question_texts.append(InternationalString(text="Quel est votre âge ?", lang="fr"))
q1.labels.append(InternationalString(text="Âge", lang="fr"))

print(f"Questions: {len(doc.questions)}")  # -> Questions: 3
print(f"Lint findings: {len(doc.lint())}")  # -> Lint findings: 0
doc.save("well-being.xml")

The count stays at 3 because both translations belong to q1. In the XML, the first question now reads:

<r:Label>
  <r:Content xml:lang="en">Age</r:Content>
  <r:Content xml:lang="fr">Âge</r:Content>
</r:Label>
<d:QuestionText>
  <d:LiteralText>
    <d:Text xml:lang="en" isPlainText="true">What is your age?</d:Text>
  </d:LiteralText>
  <d:LiteralText>
    <d:Text xml:lang="fr">Quel est votre âge ?</d:Text>
  </d:LiteralText>
</d:QuestionText>

items.title: Quiz
items.text:
Question 1 (O1): You run doc = ddi.new_study(title='Sleep Survey') and get a TypeError. Why?

B. ddi.new_study() requires both title= and agency=. The error message says so: "missing 1 required keyword-only argument: 'agency'".

Question 2 (O1): After q1 = doc.add_question(text='What is your age?'), what is q1?

C. doc.add_question() adds a question item to the study and returns that question object. Keeping it in a variable lets you work with it later.

Question 3 (O2): A study has three questions. You add a fourth with doc.add_question(), then run print(len(doc.questions)). What is printed?

A. doc.questions is the list of every question in the study, and len() counts them: three plus the new one.

Question 4 (O3): You open the file written by doc.save('well-being.xml'). Where do you find the text of your first question?

A. doc.save() writes the whole study, and each question's text sits in <d:Text>, inside <d:LiteralText>, inside <d:QuestionText>.

Question 5 (O4): You want the first question, q1, in both English and French. Which line does it?

C. Appending an InternationalString with the new language stores both versions in the same question item. Option A creates a brand-new, separate question, not a translation of q1.

Question 6 (O5): doc.validate() returns an empty list, but doc.lint() reports warnings. Is the document valid DDI?

D. An empty list from doc.validate() means the document follows the DDI schema. Lint warnings are worth fixing, but they do not make the document invalid.

Question 7 (O5): doc.lint() reports 'Maintainable element is missing a label.' once for each of your three questions. Which change clears the warnings?

B. The warning names the problem: the questions have no label. Saving or validating does not change the document, and adding the questions again with the same code brings the same warnings back.

items.title: Module 4: Add variables and link them to questions
Exercises
items.text:
Exercise 1

For example: "A variable is one column of a data file, such as SleepHours, which holds every student's answer to the same question: how many hours they sleep per night."

Exercise 2

import ddi_l as ddi

doc = ddi.new_study(title="Student Well-Being Survey", agency="university.edu")

q1 = doc.add_question(text="What is your age?", label="Age")
q2 = doc.add_question(text="How would you rate your health?", label="Self-rated health")
q3 = doc.add_question(
    text="How many hours do you sleep per night?", label="Hours of sleep"
)

v1 = doc.add_variable(name="Age", label="Age in years", question=q1)
v2 = doc.add_variable(
    name="HealthRating", label="Self-rated health, 1 to 5", question=q2
)
v3 = doc.add_variable(name="SleepHours", label="Hours of sleep per night", question=q3)

print(f"Schema problems: {len(doc.validate())}")  # -> Schema problems: 0
print(f"Lint findings: {len(doc.lint())}")  # -> Lint findings: 0

If doc.lint() reports "Maintainable element is missing a label.", one of your questions or variables has no label=.

Exercise 3

print(f"Variables: {len(doc.variables)}")  # -> Variables: 3
for v in doc.variables:
    print(v.identifier)

Each identifier is a UUID, such as a1b2c3d4-....

Exercise 4

For example: "The link leads to the question 'How would you rate your health?', so my colleague knows the values are each student's own rating of their health. Without it, they might guess wrongly, for example that the values were measured by a doctor, or that 1 means the best health."

Exercise 5

doc.save("well-being.xml")
print(q1.identifier)

The variable's name is in <l:VariableName>:

<l:VariableName>
  <r:String xml:lang="en">Age</r:String>
</l:VariableName>

The <r:ID> inside the <r:QuestionReference> a few lines below is the same identifier that print(q1.identifier) shows. That shared identifier is the link from the variable to the question.

items.title: Quiz
items.text:
Question 1 (O1): In a table with the columns Age, HealthRating, and SleepHours, which of these is a variable?

C. A variable is like a column. Each column holds one type of information, such as a health rating, for every person in the dataset. A row is one person; a value is one answer.

Question 2 (O2): What happens when you run doc.add_variable(name='Age', question='What is your age?')?

B. question= needs the object that doc.add_question() returned. A plain string is not a question, so the call fails with an AttributeError. Pass q1 instead.

Question 3 (O2): What does question=q2 do in doc.add_variable(name='HealthRating', question=q2)?

A. The question= argument stores a link between the variable and the question that collected the data. You can see it in the XML as <r:QuestionReference>.

Question 4 (O3): Which code prints the identifier of every variable in the study?

D. doc.variables is a list, so you loop through it and print each variable's identifier. Option A fails because a list has no identifier, and option C loops through the questions, not the variables.

Question 5 (O4): A data user sees the column SleepHours and wants to know exactly what was asked. How does the link from the variable to its question help?

B. This is traceability: the link takes the user from the data column back to the exact question that collected the data.

Question 6 (O5): In the saved XML, which element links a variable to the question that collected it?

C. <r:QuestionReference> sits inside the <l:Variable> element and holds the question's identifier. <l:VariableName> holds the variable's name, and <d:QuestionText> belongs to the question itself.

items.title: Module 5: Organize with concepts and universes
Exercises
items.text:
Exercise 1

  • Nutrition: concept.
  • Adults aged 18+ in Canada: universe.
  • Sleep quality: concept.
  • Public schools in Ontario: universe.
  • Employment: concept.
  • Children aged 6 to 11 living in private households: universe.

A concept is the idea that a variable measures, such as "Nutrition". A universe is the group of people or things a study covers, such as "Adults aged 18+ in Canada".

Exercise 2

import ddi_l as ddi

doc = ddi.new_study(title="National Health Survey", agency="ca.healthcan")

demo = doc.add_concept(name="Demographics")
activity = doc.add_concept(name="Physical Activity")
nutrition = doc.add_concept(name="Nutrition")

doc.add_universe(name="Adults aged 18+ in Canada")

print(f"Concepts: {len(doc.concepts)}")  # -> Concepts: 3
print(f"Universes: {len(doc.universes)}")  # -> Universes: 1

Exercise 3

q1 = doc.add_question(text="How old are you?")
q2 = doc.add_question(text="What is your weight in kg?")
q3 = doc.add_question(text="How many days per week do you exercise?")
q4 = doc.add_question(text="How many servings of fruit do you eat per day?")

doc.add_variable(name="Age", question=q1, concept=demo)
weight = doc.add_variable(name="Weight", question=q2, concept=demo)
doc.add_variable(name="ExerciseFrequency", question=q3, concept=activity)
doc.add_variable(name="FruitServings", question=q4, concept=nutrition)

linked = weight.concept_references[0].identifier == demo.identifier

print(f"Questions: {len(doc.questions)}")  # -> Questions: 4
print(f"Variables: {len(doc.variables)}")  # -> Variables: 4
print(f"Weight is linked to Demographics: {linked}")
print(f"Schema problems: {len(doc.validate())}")  # -> Schema problems: 0

Exercise 4

print("Concepts:")
for concept in doc.concepts:
    print(f"  {concept.names[0].text}")

print("Universes:")
for universe in doc.universes:
    print(f"  {universe.names[0].text}")

items.title: Quiz
items.text:
Question 1 (O1): Which phrase is the universe of this study?

A. The universe says who is studied. "Sleep quality" and "Stress" say what is measured, so they are concepts. A question is neither.

Question 2 (O1): Which sentence correctly explains a concept?

C. A concept is an abstract idea that variables measure. Option A describes a universe, and option B describes a code list.

Question 3 (O2): What does this code print?

D. Two calls to doc.add_concept() add two concepts, and one call to doc.add_universe() adds one universe.

Question 4 (O3): The variable Age is not linked to its concept. Which call fixes it?

B. Pass the concept with concept= when you call doc.add_variable(). The other calls do not exist.

Question 5 (O4): Which loop prints the name of every universe?

C. Each universe keeps its name in names; names[0].text is the text. Option A prints the whole object, option B fails because a list has no names, and option D loops over the concepts.

items.title: Module 6: Open, modify, and re-save existing DDI files
Exercises
items.text:
Exercise 1

import ddi_l as ddi

# Create and save
doc = ddi.new_study(title="Census 2024", agency="ca.statcan")
q1 = doc.add_question(text="What is your age?")
q2 = doc.add_question(text="What is your gender?")
v1 = doc.add_variable(name="Age", question=q1)
v2 = doc.add_variable(name="Gender", question=q2)
doc.save("census-2024.xml")
print("Saved.")

# Re-open and inspect
doc2 = ddi.open_ddi("census-2024.xml")
print(f"Questions: {len(doc2.questions)}")  # -> Questions: 2
print(f"Variables: {len(doc2.variables)}")  # -> Variables: 2

Exercise 2

try:
    ddi.open_ddi("census-2024-broken.xml", validate=True)
except ddi.DDIValidationError as error:
    print(f"Not valid: {error}")

unchecked = ddi.open_ddi("census-2024-broken.xml")
print(f"Opened without checking: {len(unchecked.questions)} questions")

The path after at points to the Version element directly under DDIInstance. Its value, one, does not match the pattern for versions: [0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)* means digits, optionally followed by more groups of a dot and digits, such as 1 or 1.0.0.

Without validate=True, the broken file opens with no complaint. Only validation tells you that the file breaks the DDI rules.

Exercise 3

q3 = doc2.add_question(text="What is your marital status?")
q4 = doc2.add_question(text="How many people live in your household?")
v3 = doc2.add_variable(name="MaritalStatus", question=q3)
v4 = doc2.add_variable(name="HouseholdSize", question=q4)

doc2.questions[0].question_texts[0].text = "What was your age at your last birthday?"

statuses = doc2.add_code_list(name="Marital Status Codes")
v3.set_coded(statuses)

errors = doc2.validate()
if errors:
    print("Validation errors:", errors)
else:
    print("Document is valid.")
    doc2.save("census-2024-updated.xml")
    print("Saved updated file.")

Exercise 4

doc3 = ddi.open_ddi("census-2024-updated.xml")
print(f"Questions: {len(doc3.questions)}")  # -> Questions: 4
print(f"Variables: {len(doc3.variables)}")
print(f"Code lists: {len(doc3.code_lists)}")
print(f"First question: {doc3.questions[0].question_texts[0].text}")

original = ddi.open_ddi("census-2024.xml")
print(f"Original questions: {len(original.questions)}")

The counts grew in the new file, and the original kept its two questions: saving under a new filename left it untouched.

Exercise 5

partner = ddi.open_ddi("census-2024-partner.xml", validate=True)
partner.add_variable(name="Region")
partner.save("census-2024-partner-updated.xml")

saved = Path("census-2024-partner-updated.xml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
print("Persons living in private households" in saved)  # -> True

The element survives: ddi-l keeps XML it does not model exactly as it was, so opening and saving a file never deletes content you did not touch. This is the round-trip guarantee.

items.title: Quiz
items.text:
Question 1 (O1): What does this code print for a file with 3 questions and 5 variables?

D. ddi.open_ddi() reads the whole file. doc.questions and doc.variables list its questions and variables, in that order in the print() call.

Question 2 (O2): What is wrong with this file?

B. The path after at names the element: Version, under DDIInstance. The first part of the message says its value does not match the pattern for version numbers.

Question 3 (O3): Which line codes the variable v with the code list levels?

C. set_coded() is a method of the variable, and it takes the code list as its argument. doc.add_code_list() creates a new list; it does not code a variable.

Question 4 (O4): What does my-study.xml contain afterwards?

A. Changes live only in memory until you call doc.save(). The file on disk is unchanged.

Question 5 (O5): What happens to an element that ddi-l does not model?

D. This is the round-trip guarantee: content that ddi-l does not recognize passes through the read-and-write cycle untouched.

items.title: Module 7: Validate from the command line
Exercises
items.text:
Exercise 1

ddi validate census-2024.xml

The output says Document is valid., so the file follows all the DDI schema rules.

Exercise 2

cp census-2024.xml broken.xml
# edit line 5 of broken.xml, then:
ddi validate broken.xml
  • What: the value one does not match the pattern for versions. [0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)* means digits, optionally followed by more groups of a dot and digits, such as 1 or 1.0.0.
  • Where: the path after at ends with DDIInstance, then Version: the Version element directly under the root, which is the one on line 5. The context: line confirms the value found: one.

Exercise 3

ddi lint census-2024.xml --format table

One finding: severity warning, rule ddi.maintainable.labels, message "Maintainable element is missing a label." The file has four of them: its two questions and two variables have no label. To fix them, pass label= when you add each item, as in Section 9 of Module 3. The file is still valid: warnings point to quality, not to schema errors.

Exercise 4

ddi to-json census-2024.xml --indent 2 --output census-2024.json
wc -l census-2024.json

The wc -l command counts the number of lines in a file (on Windows PowerShell, use (Get-Content census-2024.json).Count). A file with two questions and two variables gives about 200 lines; more content gives more lines.

Exercise 5

ddi roundtrip census-2024.xml --output census-2024-roundtrip.xml
ls -l census-2024.xml census-2024-roundtrip.xml

The ls -l command shows the file sizes (use dir on Windows). The copy is the same file, byte for byte: ddi-l writes back what it did not change as it was read, whichever tool wrote the file. To lay it out in this library's format instead, add --layout default; a file from another tool may then change size, because of spacing.

Exercise 6

ddi validate census-2024.xml
echo $?
ddi validate broken.xml
echo $?
# edit line 5 of broken.xml back to <r:Version>1</r:Version>, then:
ddi validate broken.xml
echo $?

A valid file gives exit code 0. A file with a schema error gives 1, and the fixed file gives 0 again, with Document is valid. above it. A script that runs ddi validate can use these codes to stop before it publishes a broken file.

items.title: Quiz
items.text:
Question 1 (O1): What does this output tell you?

A. ddi validate checks the schema only. Lint findings are a separate check (ddi lint), so option B does not follow.

Question 2 (O2): Where is the problem in this output?

C. The path after at ends with QuestionItem[1], the first question item, which holds the problem; the message names the unexpected element. A file that is not well-formed gives a mismatched tag error instead.

Question 3 (O3): What do these two results tell you about the file?

B. Validation checks the schema; lint checks quality rules beyond it. A warning alone does not fail ddi lint: it returns 0 unless you pass --fail-severity warning.

Question 4 (O4): Which command writes a JSON copy of my-study.xml to my-study.json?

D. ddi to-json converts DDI XML to JSON, and --output saves it in a file. ddi roundtrip writes XML, and the ddi validate command in option B saves the validation report, not the document.

Question 5 (O4): Why would you run ddi roundtrip on a file from another tool?

B. A round-trip writes back what it did not change as it was read, so an identical copy shows nothing was lost; --layout default lays the file out afresh. ddi-l keeps the elements it does not model, so nothing is deleted.

Question 6 (O5): What does this script print?

C. ddi validate returns 1 when the file has any schema error, however many there are. The exit code says "failed", not how many problems were found.

items.title: Module 8: From a CSV or Excel table to DDI
Exercises
items.text:
Exercise 1

import csv
import ddi_l as ddi

with open("survey_sample.csv") as f:
    reader = csv.DictReader(f)
    columns = reader.fieldnames

# The question each column records, worded the way respondents saw it
QUESTIONS = {
    "age": "How old are you?",
    "gender": "What is your gender?",
    "income": "What was your total income last year, before taxes?",
    "education_level": "What is the highest level of education you have completed?",
}

doc = ddi.new_study(title="Household Survey", agency="research.org")
for col in columns:
    wording = QUESTIONS.get(col)
    # A column nobody was asked about, such as respondent_id, gets no question
    q = doc.add_question(text=wording) if wording else None
    doc.add_variable(name=col, question=q)

doc.save("household-survey.xml")
print(f"Variables: {len(doc.variables)}")  # -> Variables: 5

Exercise 2

Only the lines that read the column names change. QUESTIONS is the lookup table from Exercise 1.

import pandas as pd
import ddi_l as ddi

# Make a workbook from the sample CSV (once)
pd.read_csv("survey_sample.csv").to_excel("survey_sample.xlsx", index=False)

df = pd.read_excel("survey_sample.xlsx")
columns = list(df.columns)

doc = ddi.new_study(title="Household Survey", agency="research.org")
for col in columns:
    wording = QUESTIONS.get(col)
    q = doc.add_question(text=wording) if wording else None
    doc.add_variable(name=col, question=q)
doc.save("household-survey-excel.xml")
print(f"Variables: {len(doc.variables)}")

Exercise 3

Continuing from Exercise 1 (columns and QUESTIONS):

doc = ddi.new_study(title="Household Survey", agency="research.org")

demo = doc.add_concept(name="Demographics")
econ = doc.add_concept(name="Economics")
educ = doc.add_concept(name="Education")
doc.add_universe(name="Canadian households, 2024")

CONCEPTS = {
    "age": demo,
    "gender": demo,
    "income": econ,
    "education_level": educ,
}

for col in columns:
    wording = QUESTIONS.get(col)
    q = doc.add_question(text=wording) if wording else None
    doc.add_variable(name=col, question=q, concept=CONCEPTS.get(col))

linked = [v for v in doc.variables if v.concept_references]
print(f"Concepts: {len(doc.concepts)}")  # -> Concepts: 3
print(f"Universes: {len(doc.universes)}")  # -> Universes: 1
print(f"Linked variables: {len(linked)}")  # -> Linked variables: 4

Exercise 4

from pathlib import Path

from ddi_l.models.base import InternationalString

# The first question asks for the respondent's age, the second for their gender
doc.questions[0].question_texts.append(
    InternationalString(text="Quel âge avez-vous ?", lang="fr")
)
doc.questions[1].question_texts.append(
    InternationalString(text="Quel est votre genre ?", lang="fr")
)
doc.concepts[0].names.append(
    InternationalString(text="Démographie", lang="fr", child_tag="String")
)
doc.save("household-survey-bilingual.xml")

saved = Path("household-survey-bilingual.xml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
print("How old are you?" in saved, "Quel âge avez-vous ?" in saved)  # -> True True

You can also open the XML in a text editor and look for xml:lang="fr" next to the English text.

Exercise 5

The message names the lang attribute and its value, fr_CA. The pattern [a-zA-Z]{1,8}(-[a-zA-Z0-9]{1,8})* means letters, optionally followed by groups of a hyphen and letters or digits. An underscore is not allowed, so write fr-CA (or just fr):

doc.questions[2].question_texts[-1].lang = "fr-CA"

issues = doc.validate()
if issues:
    for issue in issues:
        print(issue.message)
else:
    print("Document is valid.")  # -> Document is valid.
    doc.save("household-survey-bilingual.xml")

items.title: Quiz
items.text:
Question 1 (O1): How many variables does the document hold?

D. The loop adds one variable per column, and there are three columns. A column with no question, such as id, still gets a variable.

Question 2 (O1): Why does the script take question text from the QUESTIONS lookup table?

B. A column name such as education_level is shorthand. The question text in DDI should be the wording from the questionnaire.

Question 3 (O2): How do you get column names from a pandas DataFrame?

C. Use df.columns to get the column names from a pandas DataFrame. Wrap it in list() to get a plain list. fieldnames belongs to csv.DictReader, not to pandas.

Question 4 (O3): Which call adds the income variable and links it to the Economics concept econ?

A. Pass the concept with concept= when you add the variable. In a loop, concept=CONCEPTS.get(col) does the same for every column.

Question 5 (O4): How can you confirm that French wording was saved?

D. The saved XML is what other people receive, so check it: open it in a text editor, or read it with Path(...).read_text() and test "Quel âge avez-vous ?" in saved. The CSV holds data, not metadata.

Question 6 (O5): doc.validate() reports this issue. What is the fix?

A. The pattern allows letters joined by hyphens, not underscores. A schema issue makes the document invalid, so fix it before you save.

items.title: Module 9: Build code lists and controlled vocabularies
Exercises
items.text:
Exercise 1

A sample answer: "A code list is the fixed set of allowed answers to a question, and each allowed answer (such as Employed or Retired) is a category. If the census uses the same code list as the labour survey, every answer falls into the same categories in both, so we can count and compare them directly instead of cleaning free text such as 'M', 'emp.' or 'working'."

Exercise 2

import ddi_l as ddi
from ddi_l.models.logicalproduct import Category

doc = ddi.new_study(title="National Census", agency="ca.statcan")

doc.add_code_list(name="Gender Codes")
doc.add_item(Category, name="Male")
doc.add_item(Category, name="Female")
doc.add_item(Category, name="Other")

doc.add_code_list(name="Employment Status Codes")
doc.add_item(Category, name="Employed")
doc.add_item(Category, name="Unemployed")
doc.add_item(Category, name="Retired")
doc.add_item(Category, name="Student")

doc.add_code_list(name="Housing Type Codes")
doc.add_item(Category, name="House")
doc.add_item(Category, name="Apartment")
doc.add_item(Category, name="Other Housing")

print(f"Code lists: {len(doc.code_lists)}")
print(f"Categories: {len(doc.items(Category))}")

Exercise 3

for cat in doc.items(Category):
    print(cat.names[0].text)

The categories come back in the order you added them.

Exercise 4

doc.add_code_list(name="Marital Status Codes")
for status in ("Single", "Married", "Separated", "Widowed"):
    doc.add_item(Category, name=status)

print(f"Code lists: {len(doc.code_lists)}")
print(f"Categories: {len(doc.items(Category))}")

One new code list makes 3 + 1 = 4. Four new categories make 10 + 4 = 14. The counts cover the whole document, not just the list you added last.

Exercise 5

Python's built-in csv module is enough; a set keeps one copy of each value:

import csv

with open("survey_sample.csv") as f:
    levels = sorted({row["education_level"] for row in csv.DictReader(f)})

doc.add_code_list(name="Education Level Codes")
for level in levels:
    doc.add_item(Category, name=level)

print(f"Education levels: {len(levels)}")

The file has five rows but only four distinct levels, because "Bachelor" appears twice. With pandas, df["education_level"].dropna().unique() gives the same values, as in Section 7.

items.title: Quiz
items.text:
Question 1 (O1): Why is Survey 2 easier to compare?

D. A code list fixes the allowed answers. Two surveys that share it put every answer into the same categories, so their counts line up. Free text such as "M", "emp." or "working" has to be cleaned first.

Question 2 (O2): Which fix makes this script run?

A. Category is a class that you import before you use it. doc.add_category() does not exist, add_code_list() would create a code list called "Male", and add_item() needs the class itself, not its name as a string.

Question 3 (O3): What does this script print?

C. The script creates two code lists and five categories. items(Category) counts every category in the document, whichever list you meant it for.

Question 4 (O3): Which loop prints the name of every category in doc?

B. doc.items(Category) returns every category, and names[0].text is the first name of each one. Option A prints the code list names, doc.categories does not exist, and items() takes the class, not a string.

Question 5 (O4): How many categories does a CSV column give?

A. The distinct non-blank values are Female, Male and Other. With pandas, df["gender"].dropna().unique() returns exactly those three.

items.title: Module 10: Map a questionnaire to DDI flow logic
Exercises
items.text:
Exercise 1

  • Intro → a StatementItem.
  • T1, T2 and T3 → one question each, wrapped in a QuestionConstruct.
  • "ask only if T1 = Yes" → an IfThenElse whose condition tests T1 and whose "then" branch runs T2's QuestionConstruct.
  • "repeat for each trip" → a Loop that points to T3's QuestionConstruct (or to a Sequence that holds it).
  • The order of the steps → the main Sequence.
  • The whole questionnaire → an Instrument that points to the main Sequence.

Exercise 2

import ddi_l as ddi
from ddi_l.models.datacollection import QuestionConstruct, Sequence

doc = ddi.new_study(title="National Health Survey", agency="ca.healthcan")
q_age = doc.add_question(text="What is your age?")
q_gender = doc.add_question(text="What is your gender?")
q_employed = doc.add_question(text="Are you currently employed?")
q_occupation = doc.add_question(text="What is your occupation?")
q_health = doc.add_question(text="How would you rate your general health?")
q_smoke = doc.add_question(text="Do you smoke?")

qc_age = doc.add_item(
    QuestionConstruct, name="Ask Age", question_reference=q_age.to_reference()
)
qc_gender = doc.add_item(
    QuestionConstruct, name="Ask Gender", question_reference=q_gender.to_reference()
)
qc_employed = doc.add_item(
    QuestionConstruct,
    name="Ask Employed",
    question_reference=q_employed.to_reference(),
)
qc_occupation = doc.add_item(
    QuestionConstruct,
    name="Ask Occupation",
    question_reference=q_occupation.to_reference(),
)
qc_health = doc.add_item(
    QuestionConstruct, name="Ask Health", question_reference=q_health.to_reference()
)
qc_smoke = doc.add_item(
    QuestionConstruct, name="Ask Smoke", question_reference=q_smoke.to_reference()
)

seq_demographics = doc.add_item(
    Sequence,
    name="Section A - Demographics",
    control_construct_references=[qc_age.to_reference(), qc_gender.to_reference()],
)
seq_employment = doc.add_item(
    Sequence,
    name="Section B - Employment",
    control_construct_references=[qc_employed.to_reference()],
)
seq_health = doc.add_item(
    Sequence,
    name="Section C - Health",
    control_construct_references=[qc_health.to_reference(), qc_smoke.to_reference()],
)

print(f"QuestionConstructs: {len(doc.items(QuestionConstruct))}")
print(f"Sequences: {len(doc.items(Sequence))}")
print(f"Steps in Section A: {len(seq_demographics.control_construct_references)}")

Exercise 3

from ddi_l.models.datacollection import IfThenElse

skip_employment = doc.add_item(IfThenElse, name="Age gate for employment")
skip_employment.set_condition("age >= 16", description="Working age")
skip_employment.then_construct_reference = seq_employment.to_reference()

ask_occupation = doc.add_item(IfThenElse, name="Occupation routing")
ask_occupation.set_condition("employed == 1", description="Employed")
ask_occupation.then_construct_reference = qc_occupation.to_reference()
seq_employment.control_construct_references.append(ask_occupation.to_reference())

print(f"IfThenElse: {len(doc.items(IfThenElse))}")
print(f"Steps in Section B: {len(seq_employment.control_construct_references)}")

Exercise 4

from ddi_l.models.datacollection import Loop

roster_loop = doc.add_item(Loop, name="Household roster loop")
roster_loop.control_construct_reference = seq_demographics.to_reference()
roster_loop.set_condition("member <= household_size", description="Each member")

print(f"Loops: {len(doc.items(Loop))}")
repeats_a = (
    roster_loop.control_construct_reference.identifier == seq_demographics.identifier
)
print(f"Repeats Section A: {repeats_a}")

Exercise 5

from ddi_l.models.datacollection import Instrument, StatementItem

intro_a = doc.add_item(StatementItem, name="Welcome")
intro_a.set_text("Welcome to the National Health Survey")
main_seq = doc.add_item(
    Sequence,
    name="Main Survey Flow",
    control_construct_references=[
        intro_a.to_reference(),
        seq_demographics.to_reference(),
        skip_employment.to_reference(),
        seq_health.to_reference(),
        roster_loop.to_reference(),
    ],
)
instrument = doc.add_item(Instrument, name="Health Survey Instrument")
instrument.control_construct_reference = main_seq.to_reference()

print(f"Steps in main flow: {len(main_seq.control_construct_references)}")
print(f"Instruments: {len(doc.items(Instrument))}")
print(f"Validation errors: {len(doc.validate())}")

Exercise 6

Answers vary. Check that every QuestionConstruct references a question, that each Sequence lists its steps in the order respondents see them, and that the Instrument points to the top-level Sequence. Run doc.validate() before you save: it should return [].

items.title: Quiz
items.text:
Question 1 (O1): Which constructs does this spec line need?

A. "Ask only if" is a condition, so it is an IfThenElse. Its "then" branch runs the QuestionConstruct that asks B2.

Question 2 (O2): What is wrong with this Sequence?

C. A Sequence orders control constructs. The question holds the content; the QuestionConstruct is the instruction "ask it now", and that is what a Sequence lists.

Question 3 (O3): A 12-year-old reaches this gate. What happens next?

D. The condition age >= 16 is false, and the gate has no "else" branch, so nothing runs inside it. The main Sequence then moves on to its next step, Section C.

Question 4 (O4): Which line makes the roster repeat Section A?

B. A Loop points to the one construct it repeats through control_construct_reference. Option A would put the loop inside Section A, which is the wrong way round.

Question 5 (O5): What if the Instrument is not linked to the flow?

C. The schema does not require the link, so the file is valid. But only control_construct_reference connects the questionnaire's entry point to the flow. Always set it, then validate.

items.title: Module 11: Document data files and variable lineage
Exercises
items.text:
Exercise 1

A sample answer: "The collection file holds the raw answers exactly as respondents gave them, such as age and health_rating. The production file keeps those cleaned variables and adds derived ones computed from them, such as age_group and health_score. The master file keeps only the derived variables that are ready for release, and it is the file the public receives."

Exercise 2

import ddi_l as ddi
from ddi_l.models.logicalproduct import Category

doc = ddi.new_study(title="National Health Survey", agency="ca.healthcan")

q_age = doc.add_question(text="What is your age?")
q_gender = doc.add_question(text="What is your gender?")
q_employed = doc.add_question(text="Are you currently employed?")
q_occupation = doc.add_question(text="What is your occupation?")
q_health = doc.add_question(text="How would you rate your general health?")
q_smoke = doc.add_question(text="Do you smoke?")

v_age = doc.add_variable(name="age", question=q_age)
v_gender = doc.add_variable(name="gender", question=q_gender)
v_employed = doc.add_variable(name="employed", question=q_employed)
v_occupation = doc.add_variable(name="occupation", question=q_occupation)
v_health = doc.add_variable(name="health_rating", question=q_health)
v_smoke = doc.add_variable(name="smoker", question=q_smoke)

print(f"Questions: {len(doc.questions)}")
print(f"Variables: {len(doc.variables)}")
print(f"age question references: {len(v_age.question_references)}")

Exercise 3

v_age.set_numeric("Integer", low=0, high=120)

cl_gender = doc.add_code_list(name="Gender Codes")
for name in ("Male", "Female", "Other"):
    doc.add_item(Category, name=name)
v_gender.set_coded(cl_gender)

v_occupation.set_text()

rep = v_age.variable_representation
print(f"age: {rep.numeric_representation.numeric_type_code}")
rep = v_gender.variable_representation
print(f"gender is coded: {rep.code_representation is not None}")
rep = v_occupation.variable_representation
print(f"occupation is text: {rep.text_representation is not None}")

gender gets a code list because its answers come from a fixed set. occupation is text because any job title is possible.

Exercise 4

cl_age_group = doc.add_code_list(name="Age Group Codes")
for group in ("0-15", "16-24", "25-44", "45-64", "65+"):
    doc.add_item(Category, name=group)

v_age_group = doc.add_variable(name="age_group", question=q_age)
v_age_group.set_coded(cl_age_group)
v_age_group.source_variable_references = [v_age.to_reference()]

v_emp_code = doc.add_variable(name="employment_status_code", question=q_employed)
v_emp_code.source_variable_references = [v_employed.to_reference()]

v_health_score = doc.add_variable(name="health_score", question=q_health)
v_health_score.source_variable_references = [v_health.to_reference()]

print(f"Variables: {len(doc.variables)}")

Exercise 5

v_master_ag = doc.add_variable(name="age_group_master", question=q_age)
v_master_ag.source_variable_references = [v_age_group.to_reference()]

v_master_emp = doc.add_variable(name="employment_status_master", question=q_employed)
v_master_emp.source_variable_references = [v_emp_code.to_reference()]

v_master_hs = doc.add_variable(name="health_score_master", question=q_health)
v_master_hs.source_variable_references = [v_health_score.to_reference()]

print(f"Variables: {len(doc.variables)}")

for v in doc.variables:
    sources = len(v.source_variable_references)
    if sources > 0:
        print(f"  {v.names[0].text}: {sources} source(s)")

Exercise 6

v_height = doc.add_variable(name="height_cm")
v_weight = doc.add_variable(name="weight_kg")

v_bmi = doc.add_variable(name="bmi")
v_bmi.source_variable_references = [
    v_height.to_reference(),
    v_weight.to_reference(),
]

print(f"BMI sources: {len(v_bmi.source_variable_references)}")

Exercise 7

current = v_master_hs
print(current.names[0].text)
while current.source_variable_references:
    current = doc.find(current.source_variable_references[0].identifier)
    print(current.names[0].text)

question = doc.find(current.question_references[0].identifier)
print(question.question_texts[0].text)

The loop stops at health_rating, the collection variable. Only its question link is left to follow.

items.title: Quiz
items.text:
Question 1 (O1): Which file is this?

D. The master file keeps only the final derived variables, ready for dissemination. The production file would also hold age, gender and employed.

Question 2 (O2): Which call fits this variable?

A. The values are whole numbers you can add and average, so the representation is numeric, with the valid range. A code list of 366 categories would hide that, and text would allow "three" or "a few".

Question 3 (O3): How do you record that smoker came from q_smoke?

B. The question= parameter adds the link to question_references. source_variable_references is for source variables, not questions.

Question 4 (O4): A BMI variable is computed from height and weight. How many source_variable_references does it have?

C. BMI has 2 source variable references, one for height and one for weight, because it is derived from both.

Question 5 (O4): What does source_variable_references track?

B. source_variable_references is a list of references pointing to the variables that were used to compute a derived variable. Questions go in question_references, and the code list in the representation.

Question 6 (O5): What does this code print?

A. The loop follows health_score_master → health_score → health_rating, and stops there because health_rating has no source variable. It prints a variable name; the question text needs one more step through question_references.

items.title: Module 12: Data linkage: combining records across datasets
Exercises
items.text:
Exercise 1

A sample answer: "Linkage combines records from the two files that describe the same person, using a variable they share. The register already holds every hospital visit, so linking gives us that information without asking respondents anything new, which reduces their burden. The counts also come from records rather than from memory, and the linked file can answer questions neither file answers alone, such as whether people who rate their health as poor visit hospital more often."

Exercise 2

  • (a) Deterministic: both files carry the same reliable ID, so an exact match on it is enough.
  • (b) Probabilistic: there is no shared ID, and the names have errors, so you weigh agreement across several quasi-identifiers and apply a threshold.
  • (c) Deterministic: the respondent ID is stable across waves.

Exercise 3

import ddi_l as ddi

doc = ddi.new_study(
    title="Canadian Community Health Survey 2021",
    agency="ca.statcan",
)
q_key = doc.add_question(text="Anonymized linkage key")
q_health = doc.add_question(text="How would you rate your general health?")
survey_key = doc.add_variable(name="anon_id", question=q_key)
survey_health = doc.add_variable(name="health_rating", question=q_health)

admin = doc.add_study(title="Hospital Admissions Register 2021")
admin_ds = doc.study(admin.identifier)
admin_key = admin_ds.add_variable(name="anon_id")
admin_visits = admin_ds.add_variable(name="hospital_visits")

print(f"Survey variables: {len(doc.variables)}")
print(f"hospital_visits found: {doc.find(admin_visits.identifier) is not None}")

doc.variables counts only the survey's two variables. The register's variables are in the second study, and doc.find() still reaches them.

Exercise 4

survey_key.set_property("linkage_role", "key")
admin_key.set_property("linkage_role", "key")

print(f"Survey anon_id: {survey_key.get_property('linkage_role')}")
print(f"Register anon_id: {admin_key.get_property('linkage_role')}")
print(f"health_rating: {survey_health.get_property('linkage_role')}")

health_rating was never tagged, so get_property() returns None.

Exercise 5

cmp = doc.add_comparison(name="Survey-to-Admin Microdata Linkage 2021")
key_match = cmp.correspondence(
    commonality="Anonymized personal identifier common to both sources.",
    weight=1.0,
)
cmp.add_variable_map(
    survey_key.to_reference(),
    admin_key.to_reference(),
    correspondence=key_match,
)
cmp.set_property("linkage_method", "deterministic")
cmp.set_property("match_rate", "0.94")

print(f"Comparisons: {len(doc.comparisons)}")
print(f"Variable maps: {len(cmp.variable_maps)}")
method = cmp.get_property("linkage_method")
print(f"{method}, match rate {cmp.get_property('match_rate')}")

Exercise 6

linked = doc.add_variable(name="health_by_hospital_use")
linked.source_variable_references = [
    survey_health.to_reference(),
    admin_visits.to_reference(),
]

print(f"Linked variable sources: {len(linked.source_variable_references)}")

Exercise 7

prob = doc.add_comparison(name="Probabilistic Linkage")
prob.set_property("linkage_method", "probabilistic")
partial = prob.correspondence(
    commonality="Agreement across date of birth, sex, and postal code.",
    weight=0.85,
)

for name in ("date_of_birth", "sex", "postal_code"):
    survey_var = doc.add_variable(name=name)
    register_var = admin_ds.add_variable(name=name)
    survey_var.set_property("linkage_role", "matching")
    register_var.set_property("linkage_role", "matching")
    prob.add_variable_map(
        survey_var.to_reference(),
        register_var.to_reference(),
        correspondence=partial,
    )

print(f"Variable maps: {len(prob.variable_maps)}")
print(prob.get_property("linkage_method"))

A weight below 1.0 records that agreement on these fields is strong evidence of a match, but not proof.

items.title: Quiz
items.text:
Question 1 (O1): Why link instead of asking a new question?

A. Linkage combines records about the same person from existing files. It reduces respondent burden and creates information that neither file holds alone. It still needs a common variable to join the records.

Question 2 (O2): Which linkage method fits these files?

B. With no reliable key and errors in some fields, an exact match on one field would miss true pairs (name typos) or join the wrong people (many share a postal code). Probabilistic linkage combines the evidence from several quasi-identifiers.

Question 3 (O3): How do you add a variable to the register study?

C. doc.study() returns a cursor for that study, and its add_* methods add items there. doc.add_variable() always adds to the primary study, the survey.

Question 4 (O4): What does this code print?

D. Only survey_key was tagged. get_property() returns the value stored under the key, or None when the item has no such key.

Question 5 (O5): Which call records that the two keys correspond exactly?

A. A variable map in the Comparison records that the survey key corresponds to the register key, and the correspondence weight 1.0 says they are the same identifier. Option B tags one side only; option C records a quality figure; option D records provenance.

Question 6 (O6): How do you record that a linked variable draws on two source files?

B. source_variable_references holds a Reference to each source variable (here, one to the survey variable and one to the admin variable), even though they live in different studies.

items.title: Module 13: Custom properties, find, remove, and validate
Exercises
items.text:
Exercise 1

import ddi_l as ddi

doc = ddi.new_study(title="Household Survey", agency="research.org")
q_age = doc.add_question(text="How old are you?")
q_income = doc.add_question(text="What is your household income?")
q_name = doc.add_question(text="What is your full name?")

q_income.set_property("sensitivity", "high")
q_name.set_property("sensitivity", "high")
q_name.set_property("data_source", "self-reported")
print(q_name.properties)
# -> {'sensitivity': 'high', 'data_source': 'self-reported'}

print(q_name.remove_property("data_source"))  # -> True
print(q_name.properties)  # -> {'sensitivity': 'high'}

Exercise 2

v_age = doc.add_variable(name="Age", question=q_age)

found = doc.find(v_age.identifier)
print(f"Found: {found.names[0].text}")  # -> Found: Age
print(doc.find("not-an-identifier"))  # -> None

doc.find() returns None when nothing matches; it does not raise an error.

Exercise 3

doc.remove(q_name.identifier)
print(f"Questions: {len(doc.questions)}")  # -> Questions: 2
print(doc.remove(q_name.identifier))  # -> False

The second call finds nothing to remove, so it returns False.

Exercise 4

doc.remove(q_age.identifier)

for finding in doc.lint():
    if finding.severity == "error":
        print(finding.rule_id)  # -> ddi.reference.integrity

v_age.question_references = [
    ref for ref in v_age.question_references if ref.identifier != q_age.identifier
]
errors = [finding for finding in doc.lint() if finding.severity == "error"]
print(f"Lint errors: {len(errors)}")  # -> Lint errors: 0

Removing the Age variable too (doc.remove(v_age.identifier)) is also a correct fix, if the variable means nothing without its question.

Exercise 5

issues = doc.validate()
print(f"Issues: {len(issues)}")  # -> Issues: 1
print(issues[0].context)  # -> <r:Version> 1.a

# A version is numbers separated by dots
q_income.version = "1.1"
issues = doc.validate()
print(f"Issues: {len(issues)}")
print(issues[0].context)  # -> <d:Text> Revenu du ménage ?

# A language tag uses a hyphen, not an underscore
q_income.question_texts[-1].lang = "fr-CA"
issues = doc.validate()
print(f"Issues: {len(issues)}")  # -> Issues: 0

doc.save("household-clean.xml")

The first run reports only the version. The language tag shows up once the version is fixed, which is why you validate again after every fix.

items.title: Quiz
items.text:
Question 1 (O1): What does print(q.properties) show after these two calls?

C. Setting a key the item already has replaces its value. An item has at most one value per key.

Question 2 (O1): Which line removes the property data_source from the item q?

A. remove_property() removes the key and returns True. B deletes the key from a new dictionary that properties built, so the item keeps it. C removes items by identifier, not properties. D only reads the value.

Question 3 (O2): doc.remove(v.identifier) just returned True. What does doc.find(v.identifier) return now?

D. The variable is no longer in the document, so nothing matches, and doc.find() returns None rather than raising an error.

Question 4 (O3): You remove a question that a variable refers to. doc.validate() returns an empty list. Is the document ready to share?

B. Validation checks the shape of the file against the schema, not whether each reference finds its target. Lint does. doc.save() warns about the broken reference but keeps it.

Question 5 (O4): Validation reports this issue. Which fix is right?

A. The message says the xml:lang value en_US does not match the allowed pattern, which uses hyphens. The context shows which text holds it. Removing the question (B) loses data to hide the problem; C and D do not change the tag.

Question 6 (O4): Validation reports this issue on a question's version. Which value passes?

C. The pattern allows numbers separated by dots, and nothing else. Validate again after the fix to confirm it, and to see any issue the first one hid.

items.title: Module 14: Custom fields: extend the standard for your organization
Exercises
items.text:
Exercise 1

import ddi_l as ddi

doc = ddi.new_study(title="Household Survey", agency="survey.example.org")
q_income = doc.add_question(text="What is your household income?")
income = doc.add_variable(name="income", question=q_income)

study = doc.study_unit
study.set_property("myorg:retention_policy", "destroy after 7 years")
study.set_property("myorg:security_class", "Confidential")
income.set_property("myorg:source_system", "CRM-2024")

print(study.properties)
print(income.get_property("myorg:source_system"))  # -> CRM-2024

The retention policy and the classification describe the whole dataset, so they go on the study. The source system describes one variable.

Exercise 2

from ddi_l.models.base import UserID

income.user_ids.append(UserID(value="CAT-000734", type_of_user_id="InternalCatalogue"))

uid = income.user_ids[0]
print(f"{uid.type_of_user_id}: {uid.value}")  # -> InternalCatalogue: CAT-000734

(a) UserID: another system can look the variable up by this number, so it identifies the item. (b) and (c) are custom properties: they describe the item.

Exercise 3

from uuid import uuid4

from ddi_l.models.logicalproduct import Category, CodeItem

# Build the controlled vocabulary. Each allowed value needs a Category (its
# meaning) AND a Code in the list that references it; a Category alone is not
# in any list. Each Code gets its own UUID4-based URN.
quality_codes = doc.add_code_list(name="Quality Flag Codes")
for value in ("validated", "provisional", "suppressed"):
    category = doc.add_item(Category, name=value)
    quality_codes.codes.append(
        CodeItem(
            agency=quality_codes.agency,
            identifier=str(uuid4()),
            version=quality_codes.version,
            value=value,
            category=category.to_reference(),
        )
    )

# A field whose value is drawn from the vocabulary, plus a field that
# references the code list defining the allowed values
income.set_property("myorg:quality_flag", "validated")
income.set_property("myorg:quality_flag_codes", quality_codes)

print(income.get_property("myorg:quality_flag"))  # -> validated
print(income.get_property("myorg:quality_flag_codes").startswith("urn:ddi:"))

Objects stay attached

Variables you hold remain the objects the document serializes, before and after save().

Exercise 4

CUSTOM_FIELDS = {
    "myorg:source_system": "The system the data was extracted from.",
    "myorg:quality_flag": "Data-quality status (see Quality Flag Codes).",
    "myorg:steward": "The team accountable for the item.",
}


def set_catalog_field(item, key, value):
    if key not in CUSTOM_FIELDS:
        raise ValueError(f"{key!r} is not in the custom-field catalog")
    item.set_property(key, value)


set_catalog_field(income, "myorg:steward", "Survey Methods")
print(income.get_property("myorg:steward"))  # -> Survey Methods

try:
    set_catalog_field(income, "myorg:stewart", "Survey Methods")
except ValueError as error:
    print(f"Refused: {error}")
# -> Refused: 'myorg:stewart' is not in the custom-field catalog

Without the guard, the typo would create a second, misspelt field that no audit or reader looks for.

Exercise 5

q_income.set_property("myorg:steward", "Survey Methods")


def items_with_custom_fields(doc, prefix="myorg:"):
    count = 0
    for collection in (doc.questions, doc.variables):
        for item in collection:
            if any(key.startswith(prefix) for key in item.properties):
                count += 1
    return count


print(f"Items with custom fields: {items_with_custom_fields(doc)}")
# -> Items with custom fields: 2

The audit counts items, not fields: the income variable carries several myorg: fields and counts once.

Exercise 6

from pathlib import Path

doc.save("household-survey.xml")

reopened = ddi.open_ddi("household-survey.xml")
print(reopened.variables[0].get_property("myorg:source_system"))  # -> CRM-2024

xml = Path("household-survey.xml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
print("<r:AttributeKey>myorg:source_system</r:AttributeKey>" in xml)  # -> True

The key sits in an r:AttributeKey, inside the r:UserAttributePair that also holds its r:AttributeValue.

items.title: Quiz
items.text:
Question 1 (O1): Which call records that the whole dataset is classified Confidential?

B. A fact about the whole dataset goes on the study, doc.study_unit. A and C put it on one item (and C drops the namespace prefix). D creates a variable, not a field.

Question 2 (O6): You save a document and search the XML for your key myorg:source_system. Where do you find it?

C. set_property writes an r:UserAttributePair with an r:AttributeKey and an r:AttributeValue, the standard's extension point for custom fields. That is why the field survives save and reopen.

Question 3 (O2): RM-2291 is the records-management system's number for a variable. Where do you record it?

A. The value identifies the variable in another system, so it is a UserID. Use a custom property when the value describes the item.

Question 4 (O3): quality_codes is a code list. What does get_property return after this call?

D. Passing a DDI item as the value stores its URN, a stable link to the code list. Properties always hold strings.

Question 5 (O4): With the catalog guard of section 8, what does set_catalog_field(income, 'myorg:stewart', 'X') do?

D. The key is not in CUSTOM_FIELDS, so the function raises before it calls set_property. The typo is caught instead of creating a misspelt field.

Question 6 (O5): A question has no properties; variable v1 has myorg:a and myorg:b; variable v2 has other:flag. What does items_with_custom_fields(doc) return?

A. Only v1 has a key that starts with myorg:. The audit counts items, not fields, so its two fields count once, and other:flag does not match the prefix.

items.title: Module 15: Update and version your documents
Exercises
items.text:
Exercise 1

import ddi_l as ddi
from ddi_l.models.base import InternationalString

doc = ddi.new_study(title="Labour Force Survey v1", agency="ca.statcan")
q1 = doc.add_question(text="What is your current employment status?")
q1.question_texts.append(
    InternationalString(
        text="Quelle est votre situation d'emploi actuelle ?", lang="fr"
    )
)
q2 = doc.add_question(text="How many hours do you work per week?")
q3 = doc.add_question(text="Do you use a fax machine at work?")
doc.add_variable(name="EMPSTAT", label="Employment status", question=q1)

doc.save("survey-v1.xml")
print(f"Saved with {len(doc.questions)} questions and {len(doc.variables)} variable.")

Exercise 2

doc = ddi.open_ddi("survey-v1.xml")
print(f"Before: {len(doc.questions)} questions")

# Add a new question
doc.add_question(text="How many hours do you sleep per night?")

# Remove the outdated fax question
fax_q = next(
    q
    for q in doc.questions
    if q.question_texts[0].text == "Do you use a fax machine at work?"
)
doc.remove(fax_q.identifier)
print(f"After: {len(doc.questions)} questions")
print(doc.validate())  # -> []

The count is the same, but the content is not: one question in, one out. survey-v1.xml on disk is unchanged until you save over it, which you will not do.

Exercise 3

(a) 4. (b) 5: the size of the change does not change the number, so the rationale of version 5 is where you say that answers are no longer comparable. (c) It raises an error: 5 is a whole-number version, and ddi-l does not make it dotted unless you pass allow_dotted=True.

check = ddi.new_study(title="Version check", agency="example.org")
question = check.add_question(text="Do you work from home?")
question.version = "3"

question.increment_version()
print(question.version)  # -> 4

question.increment_version()
print(question.version)  # -> 5

try:
    question.increment_minor_version()
except ddi.DDIModelError:
    print("Refused")  # -> Refused

Exercise 4

from ddi_l.models.base import VersionRationale

study = doc.study_unit
study.increment_version()
study.version_rationales.append(
    VersionRationale(
        descriptions=[
            InternationalString(text="Added sleep question; retired fax question")
        ]
    )
)
study.version_responsibility = "Survey Design Team"

errors = doc.validate()
if errors:
    print("Errors:", errors)
else:
    doc.save("survey-v2.xml")
    print(f"Version: {study.version}")  # -> Version: 2
    for r in study.version_rationales:
        for d in r.descriptions:
            print(f"Rationale: {d.text}")
    print(f"Responsibility: {study.version_responsibility}")

Exercise 5

doc = ddi.open_ddi("survey-v2.xml")

status_q = next(
    q
    for q in doc.questions
    if q.question_texts[0].text == "What is your current employment status?"
)
for text in status_q.question_texts:
    if text.lang == "en":
        text.text = "What was your main activity last week?"
    if text.lang == "fr":
        text.text = "Quelle était votre activité principale la semaine dernière ?"

status_q.increment_version()
status_q.version_rationales.append(
    VersionRationale(
        descriptions=[
            InternationalString(text="Aligned wording with the ILO definition")
        ]
    )
)

# Repoint the variable that references the question
for variable in doc.variables:
    variable.question_references = [
        status_q.to_reference() if ref.identifier == status_q.identifier else ref
        for ref in variable.question_references
    ]

print(f"{status_q.question_texts[0].text} (version {status_q.version})")
# -> What was your main activity last week? (version 2)
print(status_q.question_texts[1].text)

errors = [finding for finding in doc.lint() if finding.severity == "error"]
print(f"Lint errors: {len(errors)}")  # -> Lint errors: 0
doc.save("survey-v3.xml")

Skip the repointing loop once and run doc.lint(): it reports a ddi.reference.integrity error for EMPSTAT.

Exercise 6

three_way = doc.add_code_list(name="Status (3)", label="Status (3)")
add_codes(
    doc,
    three_way,
    [("1", "Employed"), ("2", "Unemployed"), ("3", "Not in labour force")],
)
four_way = doc.add_code_list(name="Status (4)", label="Status (4)")
add_codes(
    doc,
    four_way,
    [("1", "Employed"), ("2", "Unemployed"), ("3", "Student"), ("4", "Retired")],
)

empstat = next(v for v in doc.variables if v.names[0].text == "EMPSTAT")
empstat.set_coded(three_way)

# The switch
empstat.set_coded(four_way)
empstat.increment_version()
empstat.version_rationales.append(
    VersionRationale(
        descriptions=[
            InternationalString(
                text="Split 'Not in labour force' into Student and Retired"
            )
        ]
    )
)

reference = empstat.variable_representation.code_representation.code_list_reference
print(doc.find(reference.identifier).names[0].text)  # -> Status (4)
print(empstat.version)  # -> 2

The rationale is what tells a reader that last year's code 3 no longer means the same thing: the version only says that the variable changed.

items.title: Quiz
items.text:
Question 1 (O1): You opened survey-2023.xml and added two questions. Which line keeps last year's file unchanged?

C. Saving under a new name writes the update to a new file and leaves survey-2023.xml as it was. A overwrites last year's file. B checks but saves nothing; D reads a file that does not exist yet.

Question 2 (O2): A question is at version 3. You call increment_version(). What is its version now?

B. increment_version() gives the next whole number. A, C and D are dotted versions, which ddi-l never makes from a whole number unless you ask for one.

Question 3 (O2): A variable is at version 1. You call increment_subversion() with no arguments. What happens?

A. An item keeps the numbering it has. A whole-number version stays whole unless you pass allow_dotted=True, because tools that number versions 1, 2, 3 may not read a dotted one.

Question 4 (O3): Which code records why question q changed and who changed it?

B. A VersionRationale holds the reason, and version_responsibility names who made the change. A changes the label; C stores a custom field that no DDI tool reads as a rationale.

Question 5 (O4): You reworded a question and bumped its version. doc.lint() now reports ddi.reference.integrity. What do you fix?

C. A DDI reference names one exact version. After the bump, the variable's question_references still name the old one, so replace them with question.to_reference(). doc.validate() does not check references, which is why D is wrong.

Question 6 (O5): How do you switch a variable from one code list to another?

A. set_coded() replaces the variable's representation with one that references the new code list. Then give the variable its next version, record a rationale, and remove the old code list if nothing else uses it.

Question 7 (O5): A variable at version 2 changes its answers from Yes/No to Every day, Some days, Never. What do you do?

D. New answer categories change what the variable holds, so it gets its next version. The version only says that it changed; the rationale says how, and that answers are no longer comparable. B makes a whole-number version dotted; C gives two different states of the variable the same version.

items.title: Exercises
items.text:
Exercise 1

Q5 is PetAge > 10. Q6 shows when Q5 does not, including a missing age, so it is not PetAge > 10. Saying it out loud gives PetAge <= 10 or missing(PetAge), which is almost the same: the two differ only for a "don't know" answer, which is answered but has no age to compare. Optional Module 18 shows how to find such differences.

print(normal("PetAge > 10"))  # -> PetAge > 10
print(normal("not PetAge > 10"))  # -> not PetAge > 10

Had Q6 been PetAge <= 10, a respondent with no age would see neither Q5 nor Q6.

The edit fires for 35 only. For 12 the comparison is false, and for a missing age a comparison is always false. To flag a missing age, you would write a second edit with when: missing(PetAge).

Exercise 2

(a) The jump fires only on "No". A respondent who did not answer H1 does not jump, so sees H2 and H3: the gate is not Own = 2. (b) Owners only: Own = 1. The two differ only when H1 has no answer, so write the one the survey means. H4 has no gate: everyone sees it.

print(normal("not Own = 2"))  # -> not Own = 2
print(normal("Own = 1"))  # -> Own = 1

Exercise 3

The pet kind comes from a closed list, so it is a code: the question PetKind itself, with the code list Species, whose labels are in English and French. Q3's English text pipes in PetKind, and so does its French text; each shows the label of its language (check once that your tool's piped text shows labels). No derived variable is needed, since the answer already is the value.

code_lists:
  Species:
    values:
      1: {en: Dog, fr: Chien}
      2: {en: Cat, fr: Chat}
      3: {en: Bird, fr: Oiseau}

Exercise 4

spec: my-pets
version: "1"
languages: [en, fr]

code_lists:
  Species:
    values:
      1: {en: Dog, fr: Chien}
      2: {en: Cat, fr: Chat}
      3: {en: Bird, fr: Oiseau}

modules:
  - id: household
    questions:
      - id: PetCount
        domain: {numeric: {min: 0, max: 20, decimals: 0}}

  - id: pets
    gate: PetCount > 0
    questions:
      - id: PetKind
        domain: {code: {list: Species}}
      - id: PetName
        domain: {text: {max_length: 50}}
        gate: answered(PetKind)
      - id: PetAge
        domain: {numeric: {min: 0, max: 40, decimals: 0}}
      - id: VetVisits
        domain: {numeric: {min: 0, max: 50, decimals: 0}}
        gate: PetAge > 10
      - id: Toys
        domain: {numeric: {min: 0, max: 99, decimals: 0}}
        gate: not PetAge > 10

  - id: visits
    questions:
      - id: LastVisit
        domain: {date: {type: Date}}

edits:
  - id: age_over_30
    when: PetAge > 30
    module: pets
    message:
      en: Is the pet really over 30?
      fr: L’animal a-t-il vraiment plus de 30 ans ?
    severity: warning

"If 0, go to Section 3" becomes the gate of the module it skips, pets. If ddi spec validate reports a problem, its path says where: modules[1].questions[2] is the third question of the second module.

Exercise 5

Finding Wrong What to change spec.gate.missing (module pets) instrument Show pets only when PetCount > 0: wrap it in an IfThenElse with that condition. spec.domain.type (PetKind, PetName, PetAge) instrument The draft's questions have no response domain. Give PetKind the Species codes, PetName text up to 50 characters, PetAge a number from 0 to 40. spec.gate.unverifiable (PetName) neither Check by hand: the draft's condition reads answered(PetKind), the spec's gate. Nothing to change. spec.language.missing (PetAge) instrument Add the French text of the question. spec.item.extra (PetColour) spec It was added on purpose: add PetColour and its domain to the pets module of the spec, and give the spec a new version. spec.edit.unverifiable (age_range) neither Not compared. Check the edit in the instrument by hand.

Items with a new version after the two fixes: PetAge's question (new text); the PetAge construct, which refers to it; the pets sequence, which refers to the construct; the new IfThenElse for the module gate, at its first version; the main sequence, which now refers to that IfThenElse instead of to pets; and the instrument. The household sequence, the other questions and constructs, and Ask PetName keep their versions. All new and revised items share one versionDate and one responsibility.

Exercise 6

The scenario says Q6 shows when Q5 does not, so a missing age must show Q6: the spec (not PetAge > 10) is right. Change the instrument's gate. The two gates differ only for a missing age, which is why equivalent() and ddi conform treat them as different.

items.title: Quiz
items.text:
Question 1 (O2): PetAge has no answer. Which gate is true?

C. A comparison is false without an answer, so A, B and D are false, and not turns A's false into true.

Question 2 (O2): An edit check has when: PetAge > 30. A respondent skips PetAge. Does the check fire?

B. The check fires when when is true, and PetAge > 30 is false when there is no answer.

Question 3 (O3): The document says: if Q4 > 10 ask Q5, otherwise Q6. A respondent with no age must see Q6. Which gate do you write for Q6?

D. not PetAge > 10 is true when PetAge > 10 is false, including when the age is missing. A and C are false on a missing age (and C also hides Q6 from a pet aged exactly 10). A second gate reads the same in every tool, which an else branch does not.

Question 4 (O4): Why does a month need no language-specific copies of its variable?

A. One code, two labels, one variable.

Question 5 (O1): ddi spec validate prints this. What do you fix?

B. Positions count from 0, so modules[0].questions[1] is the second question of the first module, and its numeric min is above its max. ddi spec validate reports problems, not warnings: the spec does not load until you fix it.

Question 6 (O5): ddi conform reports 0 errors and 12 warnings. Is the instrument right?

D. Read the warnings: a shared module that another spec covers is a typical one, and an unverifiable gate needs a check by hand. To be sure the check is live, change one gate in a copy of the spec and expect exactly one new error.

Question 7 (O5): ddi conform reports spec.item.extra for PetColour, which the survey owner added on purpose. What do you change?

C. Here the spec is the one that is wrong: it does not list a question the survey needs. Fix the record, version it, and run the check again.

Question 8 (O5): You fix the condition of the IfThenElse that gates PetName, inside the pets sequence. Which items get a new version?

A. The changed item and every item that refers to it, up to the instrument. Items that refer to nothing you changed, such as the household sequence, keep their versions.

Track A: University Student: Document Your Thesis Dataset: Sample solution

One complete script for all the steps above, using thesis-data.csv.

import csv
from uuid import uuid4

import ddi_l as ddi
from ddi_l.models.base import InternationalString, VersionRationale
from ddi_l.models.logicalproduct import Category, CodeItem


def add_codes(doc, code_list, labels):
    """Add one Category and one Code per label, numbered from 1."""
    for number, label in enumerate(labels, start=1):
        category = doc.add_item(Category, name=label, label=label)
        code_list.codes.append(
            CodeItem(
                agency=code_list.agency,
                identifier=str(uuid4()),
                version=code_list.version,
                value=str(number),
                category=category.to_reference(),
            )
        )


with open("thesis-data.csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
columns = list(rows[0])

# Version 1
doc = ddi.new_study(title="Student Stress Survey 2024", agency="university.example.org")
# How each column was asked. StudentID is assigned and AnxietyScore is computed
# from a questionnaire, so neither gets a question of its own.
QUESTIONS = {
    "Age": "How old are you?",
    "Gender": "What is your gender?",
    "YearOfStudy": "What year of your program are you in?",
    "Program": "Which program are you enrolled in?",
    "StudyHours": "On a typical day, how many hours do you study?",
    "SleepHours": "On a typical night, how many hours do you sleep?",
    "WorkHours": "How many hours a week do you work for pay?",
    "ExerciseDays": "On how many days last week did you exercise?",
    "StressLevel": "On a scale of 1 to 10, how stressed have you felt this term?",
    "SoughtSupport": "Have you sought support from campus services this term?",
}
questions = {col: doc.add_question(text=text) for col, text in QUESTIONS.items()}
variables = {
    col: doc.add_variable(name=col, question=questions.get(col)) for col in columns
}

# One code list per coded column, from the values in the file
for col in ("Gender", "Program", "SoughtSupport"):
    code_list = doc.add_code_list(name=f"{col} Codes")
    add_codes(doc, code_list, sorted({row[col] for row in rows}))
    variables[col].set_coded(code_list)

doc.add_concept(name="Demographics")
doc.add_concept(name="Academic Workload")
doc.add_concept(name="Well-Being")
doc.add_universe(name="Undergraduate students aged 18-25")
variables["StudyHours"].set_property("dataSource", "Online survey tool")
variables["AnxietyScore"].set_property(
    "scoring", "Sum of a standard 10-item anxiety scale"
)

lint_errors = [f for f in doc.lint() if f.severity == "error"]
print(f"v1: {len(doc.validate())} validation errors, {len(lint_errors)} lint errors")
doc.save("thesis-v1.xml")

# Version 2: a derived variable and its lineage
doc = ddi.open_ddi("thesis-v1.xml")
by_name = {v.names[0].text: v for v in doc.variables}
stress_index = doc.add_variable(name="StressIndex")
stress_index.source_variable_references = [
    by_name["StressLevel"].to_reference(),
    by_name["AnxietyScore"].to_reference(),
]

study = doc.study_unit
study.increment_version()
study.version_rationales.append(
    VersionRationale(
        descriptions=[
            InternationalString(text="Added the derived StressIndex variable")
        ]
    )
)
study.version_responsibility = "Thesis Author"

lint_errors = [f for f in doc.lint() if f.severity == "error"]
print(f"v2: {len(doc.validate())} validation errors, {len(lint_errors)} lint errors")
# -> v2: 0 validation errors, 0 lint errors
doc.save("thesis-v2.xml")

Track B: Researcher: Package a Health Survey for Publication: Sample solution

import csv
from uuid import uuid4

import ddi_l as ddi
from ddi_l.models.base import InternationalString, VersionRationale
from ddi_l.models.logicalproduct import Category, CodeItem


def add_codes(doc, code_list, labels):
